# Migration Guide from version 2 to version 3

Source: https://britecharts.github.io/britecharts/docs/how-tos/migration-guide-2-to-3

:::note
Version 3.0 is in beta: `@britecharts/core`, `@britecharts/wrappers` and `@britecharts/react` publish `3.0.0-beta` releases under the `beta` tag (`npm install @britecharts/core@beta`). `3.0.0-beta.6` is the last beta before 3.0.0. The last stable release is still `britecharts@2.18.2`. This guide describes the migration to 3.0 and is kept up to date until the release.
:::

Version 3.0 of Britecharts fixes many bugs, improves loading and animation performance, and adds minor features. It also introduces breaking changes that make the components' APIs and data shapes more consistent, and moves the library to the `@britecharts` scope on npm: `britecharts` becomes `@britecharts/core`, and `britecharts-react` becomes `@britecharts/react`. Both are now written in TypeScript.

When it lands, we recommend migrating as soon as possible to get all these benefits. For that, we have prepared the following migration guide.

## Migration Steps
Most of the migration tasks involve changing accessor names, but there are also changes in how we load the modules. Follow these steps to get your application updated in no time:

### Breaking changes
1. Update the way you load the charts

We moved Britecharts internally from the outdated AMD modules into ES Modules, which changed how you will import the components. See below some examples:

```js
// Version 2
// For ES modules
import bar from 'britecharts/dist/umd/bar.min';

// For AMD and CommonJS modules
const LineChart = require('britecharts/umd/line.min');

// Version 3
// As ES modules
import { bar } from '@britecharts/core';

// As CommonJS modules
const { bar } = require('@britecharts/core');

```

The stylesheets move too. `britecharts/dist/css/britecharts.min.css` is now `@britecharts/core/dist/styles/bundle/britecharts.min.css`, and each chart's own stylesheet is under `@britecharts/core/dist/styles/charts/`.

You can also check more ways of loading (CommonJS, UMD and CDN) in the [vanilla consumer](https://github.com/britecharts/britecharts/tree/main/packages/integration/consumers/vanilla) of our integration tests, which CI runs against every change

2. Change how you show loading states

Search for any use of the 'loadingState' accessor for getting the loading state, and render the chart with 'isLoading' as true and a valid dataset (it can be empty). 

```js
// Version 2
barContainer.html(barChart.loadingState())

// Version 3
barChart
    .width(containerWidth)
    .height(300)
    .isAnimated(true)
    .isLoading(true)
    .render(barContainer, dataset);
```

3. Use 'valueLocale' to format values

You must use the 'valueLocale' accessor to set the locale object (see [the d3-format docs](https://github.com/d3/d3-format#formatLocale)) of the component´s rendered values (axes ticks, numerical values, etc.).

Before, this used to be ´locale´ in the bar, grouped bar, scatted bar, and scatter plot.

```js
// Version 2
barChart
    .locale({
        thousands: '.', 
        grouping: [3], 
        currency: ["$", ""], 
        decimal: "."
    })
    //...other configurations

// Version 3
barChart
    .valueLocale({
        thousands: '.', 
        grouping: [3], 
        currency: ["$", ""], 
        decimal: "."
    })
    //...other configurations
```

In contrast, for time series charts (lineChart, stackedAreaChart), we use 'locale' to pass the language tag for the tooltip to localize the *date*. It uses Intl.DateTimeFormat, for compatibility and support.

4. Swap the use 'xAxisCustomFormat' and 'xAxisFormat' on brush charts

Whenever you were using 'xAxisCustomFormat' in a brush chart, now you should use 'xAxisFormat', and viceversa.

```js
// Version 2
brush
    .xAxisCustomFormat('custom')
    .xAxisFormat('%A');

// Version 3
brush
    .xAxisCustomFormat('%A')
    .xAxisFormat('custom');
```

This made this configuration consistent with the line and stacked area charts.

5. Use 'numberFormat' in bar charts

Search for uses of 'valueLabelFormat' and change them to 'numberFormat':

```js
// Version 2
groupedBarChart
    .valueLabelFormat(',s')
    // other configurations

// Version 3
groupedBarChart
    .numberFormat(',s')
    // other configurations

```

The 'numberFormat' configuration is available for the bar, bullet, donut, grouped bar, stacked-bar, legend, line, mini-tooltip, and tooltip components.

6. Stop using 'aspectRatio' to set charts' dimensions

We eliminated the 'aspectRatio' accessor from our charts. Instead, use the 'width' and 'height' attributes to set a explicit size and leave the chart to respond to container width changes.

```js
// Version 2
lineChart
    .width(100)
    .aspectRatio('0.5');

// Version 3
lineChart
    .width(100)
    .height(50)
```

7. Expect the typographic minus sign in negative axis labels

Britecharts v3 runs on the current d3 modules, and d3-format changed its default minus sign from the ASCII hyphen (`-`, U+002D) to the typographic minus (`−`, U+2212). Negative values on axes and in tooltips now render with the latter.

Nothing to change unless you assert on that text — snapshot tests and string comparisons against axis labels will need updating. If you would rather keep the ASCII hyphen, set it through a value locale on the charts that have one (the bar, grouped bar, stacked bar and scatter plot). The definition needs `decimal`, `thousands`, `grouping` and `currency` as well:

```js
barChart.valueLocale({
    decimal: '.',
    thousands: ',',
    grouping: [3],
    currency: ['$', ''],
    minus: '-',
});
```

8. Use the d3 v7 modules alongside Britecharts

Britecharts v3 runs on the d3 v7 generation of the `d3-*` modules. They are dependencies of `@britecharts/core`, so installing it from npm installs them, and the ES module and `dist/umd` builds load them from there rather than bundling them. If your own code uses d3 together with Britecharts, upgrade it to v7 at the same time. The CDN builds under `dist/cdn` bundle their own copy of d3 and need nothing else on the page.

The two d3 modules Britecharts used that are now deprecated upstream, `d3-collection` and `d3-voronoi`, have been replaced internally by `d3-array` and `d3-delaunay`. They are no longer dependencies.

9. Replace the 'dataByTopic' line chart data shape

The line chart no longer accepts the `dataByTopic` array it required up to 2.10.1. It has taken a flat `data` array since then, and that is now the only shape it accepts. Passing `dataByTopic` throws.

```js
// Version 2
lineChart.datum({
    dataByTopic: [
        {
            topicName: 'San Francisco',
            topic: 123,
            dates: [
                { date: '2017-01-16T16:00:00-08:00', value: 1 },
                { date: '2017-01-17T16:00:00-08:00', value: 2 }
            ]
        }
    ]
});

// Version 3
lineChart.datum({
    data: [
        { topicName: 'San Francisco', name: 123, date: '2017-01-16T16:00:00-08:00', value: 1 },
        { topicName: 'San Francisco', name: 123, date: '2017-01-17T16:00:00-08:00', value: 2 }
    ]
});
```

One entry per point instead of points nested under each topic, and the topic identifier moves from `topic` to `name`. Britecharts groups the data internally, so nothing else about how you configure the chart changes.

If you have data in the old shape, this converts it:

```js
const toFlatData = ({ dataByTopic }) =>
    dataByTopic.flatMap((topic) =>
        topic.dates.map(({ date, value }) => ({
            topicName: topic.topicName,
            name: topic.topic,
            date,
            value,
        }))
    );
```

10. Update custom tooltip handlers on the line, stacked area, stacked bar and grouped bar charts

Every chart now dispatches `customMouseMove` with the same payload: the hovered data point, its anchor `[x, y]` in pixels relative to the chart's drawing area, the chart's `[width, height]`, and, from these four charts, the map of topic names to colours. Before, they dispatched `(dataPoint, colorMap, x, y)`. If you wire the tooltip directly, nothing changes; a handler of your own that reads the arguments by position has to take the new order. `tooltip.update` still accepts the old order in 3.x and warns once.

```js
// Version 2
lineChart.on('customMouseMove', function (dataPoint, colorMap, x, y) {
    chartTooltip.update(dataPoint, colorMap, x, y);
    trackHover(dataPoint, x);
});

// Version 3
lineChart.on('customMouseMove', function (dataPoint, [x, y], size, colorMap) {
    chartTooltip.update(dataPoint, [x, y], size, colorMap);
    trackHover(dataPoint, x);
});

// Either version
lineChart.on('customMouseMove', chartTooltip.update);
```

With that, `tooltip` and `miniTooltip` are one component: `tooltip` shows a list or a single value by the shape of the data point (or as told by `layout`), and `miniTooltip` is `tooltip().layout('single').title('').numberFormat('.2f')`. The tooltip now keeps itself inside the chart, follows the pointer (the stacked and grouped bar charts show it over a bar only), and its `tooltipOffset` default is `{ x: 0, y: 0 }` (it was `{ x: 0, y: -55 }`, for a placement that no longer exists). `xAxisValueType` defaults to `'auto'`, which shows dates as dates, numbers as numbers and category names as they are; set `'date'` or `'number'` to force one, as before. In React, `Tooltip`'s `customMouseMove` callback receives the new order, and `Tooltip` now wraps the bar, scatter plot and heatmap charts too.

11. Replace the Step chart

The Step chart is removed from every package: the `step` export of `@britecharts/core`, its `StepWrapper` and the React `Step` component, with their stylesheets and builds. A bar chart draws the same data.

12. Transpile for older browsers yourself

The builds now target ES2020 instead of ES5. Every current browser runs them as they are. If you support a browser older than that, transpile Britecharts in your own build, as you would any package that ships modern syntax.

13. Move from `britecharts-react` to `@britecharts/react`

The React components are published as `@britecharts/react`, and they work differently in a few ways you may rely on:

```js
// Version 2
import { Bar } from 'britecharts-react';

// Version 3
import { Bar } from '@britecharts/react';
```

* React 16.8 or later is required, since the components are now function components built on hooks. They have no instances any more, so a `ref` on a chart component is not accepted.
* A chart redraws only when its props change. If you update your data by mutating it in place, pass a new array or object instead.
* `data` is required. Pass `null` while it loads: the chart draws nothing until the data arrives.
* `false`, `0` and `''` now reach the chart, so `isLoading={false}` ends a loading state. Leave a prop out, or pass `undefined`, to keep the chart's default.
* PropTypes are gone. Each component's props type is exported from the package root (`BarChartProps`, `LineProps` and so on) for TypeScript projects.
* `StackedBar`'s `nameLabelFormat` prop is removed. No chart had that setting, so passing it threw.
* `axisTimeCombinations` is no longer a prop of `Line`, `StackedArea` or `Tooltip`. Import the `axisTimeCombinations` constant from the package and pass one of its values to `xAxisFormat`.

14. Label bullet charts and sparklines outside the chart

The bullet chart no longer draws a title and subtitle, and the sparkline no longer draws a title. Text drawn inside the svg cannot wrap, clips at the chart's edge and does not follow the page's typography, so these charts now draw only the data. The `customTitle` and `customSubtitle` accessors and the `title` and `subtitle` data fields of the bullet chart are removed, as are the sparkline's `titleText` and `titleTextStyle`. The React `Bullet` and `Sparkline` components drop the matching props.

Put the label in your own markup next to the chart, and give screen readers the chart's name with `a11yTitle`:

```js
// Version 2
bulletChart.customTitle('CPU 1').customSubtitle('GHz');
sparklineChart.titleText('Signups');

// Version 3
// <h3>CPU 1 <small>GHz</small></h3> above the chart's container
bulletChart.a11yTitle('CPU 1, GHz');
sparklineChart.a11yTitle('Signups');
```

The legend still draws its own labels.

15. Load one bundle instead of a file per chart

Version 2 published a UMD file for each chart, like `britecharts/dist/umd/bar.min.js`. Version 3 publishes one UMD bundle and one CDN bundle with every chart, and ES modules for bundlers. Bundlers keep only the charts you import, so a per-chart file saves nothing there. On a page with a script tag, load the CDN bundle, which includes d3, and use the `core` global:

```html
<!-- Version 2 -->
<script src="https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/britecharts/dist/umd/bar.min.js"></script>
<script>const barChart = britecharts.bar();</script>

<!-- Version 3 -->
<script src="https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/@britecharts/core/dist/cdn/bundle/core.cdn.min.js"></script>
<script>const barChart = core.bar();</script>
```

The colors come with the bundle as `core.colors`. The per-chart stylesheets under `dist/styles/charts/` are still published. `@britecharts/wrappers` and `@britecharts/react` also publish only their bundles: import the wrappers and components from the package, or use the `wrappers` and `react` globals.

The packages are ES modules (`"type": "module"`), so they load with `import` in Node as well as in bundlers. `require` still works and gets the CommonJS bundle, which is now a `.cjs` file. If you required a bundle by its path, update the extension: `@britecharts/core/dist/umd/bundle/core.bundled.min.js` is now `core.bundled.min.cjs`, and likewise for `wrappers` and `react`. The CDN bundle keeps its `.js` name.

16. Expect `null` from an accessor you have not set

An accessor that has not been set now reads `null` on every chart. Before, the same accessor read `null` on some charts and `undefined` on others: `yAxisLabel` on the grouped bar, stacked bar, scatter plot and stacked area, `xAxisLabel` on the scatter plot, `numberFormat` on the donut, line and stacked area, and `locale` on the line, stacked area and tooltip.

A truthiness check works as before. Update code that compares with `=== undefined`, and TypeScript code that annotated the old type: the getters are typed `T | null`.

```js
// Version 2
if (lineChart.numberFormat() === undefined) { /* ... */ }

// Version 3
if (lineChart.numberFormat() === null) { /* ... */ }
```

17. Name your data's keys as the charts expect

The accessors that let a chart read its data under other keys are removed: `nameLabel` and `valueLabel` on the bar chart, `groupLabel`, `nameLabel` and `valueLabel` on the grouped bar, `stackLabel`, `nameLabel` and `valueLabel` on the stacked bar, `dateLabel`, `topicLabel` and `valueLabel` on the line chart, `dateLabel`, `keyLabel` and `valueLabel` on the stacked area, and `dateLabel` and `valueLabel` on the sparkline. They warned that they were deprecated since version 2. The React components drop the matching props.

If you used them, rename the keys in your data to the ones each chart's data shape names, such as `name` and `value` for the bar chart:

```js
// Version 2
barChart.nameLabel('letter').valueLabel('frequency');
barContainer.datum([{ letter: 'A', frequency: 0.08 }]).call(barChart);

// Version 3
const data = rows.map(({ letter, frequency }) => ({ name: letter, value: frequency }));
barChart.render(barContainer, data);
```

The tooltip keeps its `dateLabel`, `nameLabel`, `topicLabel` and `valueLabel`: it reads the data points of several charts, and they use different keys.

### New features
1. Start using TypeScript with Britecharts.

You can now use Britecharts in your TypeScript projects! The packages are written in TypeScript, and their type declarations are generated from that source, so they always match what the charts do. Import the types from the package root: each chart's data shape and module type from `@britecharts/core`, and each component's props from `@britecharts/react`.

2. Stop re-rendering charts when the viewport width changes.

In version 2 and our demos, we recommended listening to viewport width changes and re-render charts with the updated container width. This wasn't necessary, as SVGs provide a viewBox property that allows us to make our charts fully responsive out of the box. That's how Britecharts works starting version 3, so say bye-bye to those window 'resize' listeners!

3. Use 'colorMap' to select the colors you want for each data category.

One common request of our users was to specify the colors for each category on the different Britecharts components. Now you can! Use the ["colorMap"](https://britecharts.github.io/britecharts/docs/API/bar#module_Bar--exports.colorMap) property to specify a hash map between category names and HEX colors.

4. Specify the duration of animations with 'animationDuration'

Most Britecharts' components have animations that you can activate with the 'isAnimated' configuration. Since version 3, you can also set the duration of those animations in milliseconds with the 'animationDuration' accessor.

5. Rely on one tooltip for every chart

`tooltip` renders the line, stacked area, stacked bar and grouped bar charts' lists and the bar, scatter plot, heatmap and donut charts' single values; `maxEntries` caps the rows, `layout` forces a layout, `xAxisValueType('category')` shows a category key as it is. `customClick` on the stacked and grouped bar charts carries the clicked bar's own data as a third argument.

6. Chart negative values

The bar, grouped bar, stacked bar and brush charts draw negative values, below or to the left of a zero baseline. They used to throw on a negative datum. The scatter plot's value axis now runs below zero when the data does, and each circle's size shows the magnitude of its value. Before, points with a negative value were not drawn.

7. Show a loading state on every chart

`isLoading` now covers every data chart, including the bullet, heatmap and scatter plot, each with a skeleton in its own shape.

8. Name your charts for screen readers

Every chart gives its svg a role and an accessible name, so a screen reader announces it as an image called, for example, "Bar chart". Set `a11yTitle` to name it after what it shows, and `a11yDescription` to add a sentence that screen readers read after the name. The React components take both as props.

```js
barChart
    .a11yTitle('Monthly visits')
    .a11yDescription('Visits doubled in May');
```

9. Draw charts with 'render', and give them a 'tooltip'

`render` draws a chart into a CSS selector, an element or a d3 selection, so a page needs no d3 code of its own. The `tooltip` setting connects and places a tooltip, and sets the labels the chart's data points need. Your version 2 code, `container.datum(data).call(chart)` and the tooltip wired by hand, keeps working.

```js
// Version 2
barChart
    .on('customMouseOver', chartTooltip.show)
    .on('customMouseMove', chartTooltip.update)
    .on('customMouseOut', chartTooltip.hide);
barContainer.datum(data).call(barChart);
barContainer.select('.metadata-group').datum([]).call(chartTooltip);

// Version 3
barChart.tooltip(miniTooltip()).render(barContainer, data);
```

## Summary of Changes
We changed many things in the third version of Britecharts; here are some summaries:

### Breaking Changes
* New monorepo organization of the code with `@britecharts/core` and `@britecharts/react` as the main packages.
* The builds target ES2020 instead of ES5.
* Runs on the d3 v7 modules; negative numbers render with the typographic minus sign.
* Removes the Step chart from every package.
* Removes the line chart's 'dataByTopic' data shape.
* Publishes one UMD bundle and one CDN bundle instead of a UMD file per chart. The per-chart stylesheets stay.
* The packages are ES modules: `import` works in Node, and the CommonJS bundles `require` loads end in `.cjs`.
* Removes the data-key accessors ('nameLabel', 'valueLabel', 'dateLabel', 'topicLabel', 'keyLabel', 'groupLabel', 'stackLabel') from the bar, grouped bar, stacked bar, line, stacked area and sparkline charts, and the matching React props. The tooltip keeps its own.
* An accessor that has not been set reads `null` on every chart, never `undefined`.
* Removes the bullet chart's title and subtitle ('customTitle', 'customSubtitle' and the 'title' and 'subtitle' data fields) and the sparkline's title ('titleText', 'titleTextStyle'), with the matching React props.
* Changes 'loadingMarkup' option into an explicit option for 'isLoading' in most of the charts.
* Adds 'valueLocale' or renames 'locale' into 'valueLocale' for formatting values in the bar chart, grouped bar chart, scatter plot, and stacked bar.
* Fixes the custom format feature in the line and stacked area chart, renaming 'xAxisFormat' into 'xAxisCustomFormat' and 'xAxisCustomFormat' into 'xAxisFormat'. The time combinations are exported as `constants.axisTimeCombinations`.
* Renames value formatting functions into 'numberFormat' in the grouped bar and stacked bar charts.
* Removed the 'aspectRatio' configuration chart from the line, scatter plot, stacked area, bullet, grouped bar, stacked bar.
* Changed 'exportChart' to return a promise.
* The line, stacked area, stacked bar and grouped bar charts dispatch 'customMouseMove' as `(dataPoint, [x, y], [width, height], colorMap)`, the same payload as every other chart; `tooltip.update` still accepts the old `(dataPoint, colorMap, x, y)` order and warns once. React's `Tooltip` passes the new order to its 'customMouseMove' callback.
* The tooltip's 'tooltipOffset' defaults to `{ x: 0, y: 0 }` and 'xAxisValueType' to 'auto'.
* The stacked and grouped bar charts show the tooltip, and dispatch 'customClick', only over a bar.
* React: the components are function components, need React 16.8 or later, redraw only when their props change, and pass `false`, `0` and `''` on to the chart. PropTypes, `StackedBar`'s `nameLabelFormat` prop and the `axisTimeCombinations` prop are removed.

### New Feature Changes
* Written in TypeScript, with type declarations generated from the source
* Negative values in the bar, grouped bar, stacked bar, brush and scatter plot charts
* Loading states on every data chart, including the bullet, heatmap and scatter plot
* Accessible names for every chart, set with 'a11yTitle' and 'a11yDescription'
* Theming with CSS custom properties, and dark mode that follows the page's `color-scheme`
* A `ScatterPlot` component in `@britecharts/react`
* `Brush` and `Heatmap` components in `@britecharts/react`, and `BrushWrapper` and `HeatmapWrapper` in `@britecharts/wrappers`, so every chart has both
* Charts are responsive by default using the viewBox property.
* Adds colorMap to all charts
* Adds 'animationDuration' option to all animated charts
* Added grid helper on charts
* Adds zoom controls for scatter plot
* Added hasMinimumValueScale parameter to autoscale Line Chart y-axis
* Rework of Line Chart animation for better performance
* Allows brush to have missing data and to be animated
* Allows for a fixed window in brush chart with 'isLocked' option
* Added Donut's hasCenterLegend to hide/show center legend
* Added Stacked Area loading state
* Added tooltip on the heatmap
* One tooltip component for every chart: 'tooltip' renders a list or a single value by the data's shape ('layout' forces one), 'miniTooltip' is its single-value preset, and React's 'Tooltip' wraps the bar, scatter plot and heatmap charts too
* The tooltip keeps itself inside the chart (flips and slides at the edges), follows the pointer, fades in and out and eases towards each position, and updates its rows in place
* Tooltip: 'xAxisValueType' gains 'category' and 'auto', 'maxEntries' caps the rows with a "+n more" row, 'show' takes the hovered point
* The stacked and grouped bar charts' 'customClick' carries the clicked bar's data

### Bug Fixes
* Fixes all critical security warnings due to dependencies
* Fixes step chart loading
* Mitigates the stacked and grouped bar charts tooltip issues
* Tooltips no longer get cut off at the chart's edges, wobble across close data points, blink when crossing bars, or catch the pointer; the scatter plot's sits beside its point and a category key no longer titles it "NaN"
* Improved Grouped bar chart animation
* Line chart animation fix on multiline
* Ordering of the horizontal bar chart elements
* Cleans up custom lines annotation text before rendering
* Fixes bullet chart issues 
* The scatter plot's trendline starts at the right height
* The brush chart honours 'locale', and the stacked area chart honours 'numberFormat'
* React: unmounting one responsive container no longer stops resizing for the others, and a chart is not drawn twice under StrictMode
* Tooltip tweaks
*Visual Fixes Summary*
* Added extended line on brush chart
* Extended line color matching ticks
* Normalized text sizes in line and stacked area charts

### Contributor's Developer Experience Changes
* Deprecated Travis into Github Actions
* Moved the tests from Karma to Vitest
* Moved from Yarn to pnpm, and the build from webpack to Vite
* Rewrote the packages in TypeScript, type-checked in CI
* Integration tests install the packed packages into vanilla, TypeScript and React projects
* Added linting and formatting for CSS and JS 
* Changed organization of tests and data builders to be colocated

---

# @britecharts/core

Source: https://britecharts.github.io/britecharts/docs/packages/core-readme

> `@britecharts/core` is the main package for the [Britecharts][homepage] charting library. Use this package directly in your JavaScript projects.

## Usage
Read the [main readme][readme] or check the [Getting Started guide][gettingStarted] to learn how to use Britecharts.

## Installation
To install run:
```sh
pnpm add @britecharts/core
```
Or, with npm:

```
npm i --save @britecharts/core
```

Britecharts is available as an [NPM module][npmModule] or through CDN links (in [different formats][jsDelivrLib] or a [bundle][jsDelivrDist]).

## Using Britecharts with a coding agent
The package ships an agent skill in `skills/britecharts`. It covers each chart's data shape and accessors, tooltip wiring, React and the wrappers, and the v2 code that no longer works in v3. Install it with the [skills CLI][skillsCli]:

```sh
npx skills add britecharts/britecharts
```

Or copy `node_modules/@britecharts/core/skills/britecharts` into your agent's skills folder, such as `.claude/skills/` for Claude Code. Agents that read [llms.txt][llmsTxt] can also load the whole documentation from [llms-full.txt][llmsFullTxt].

## See Also
- [Documentation Homepage][homepage]
- [Contributing Guide][contributing]
- [Code of Conduct][codeOfConduct]

## Contribute
Check the [contributing guide][contributing] if you want to help us bringing these in. 

[readme]: https://britecharts.github.io/britecharts/docs/Britecharts
[homepage]: https://britecharts.github.io/britecharts/
[gettingStarted]: https://britecharts.github.io/britecharts/docs/tutorials/getting-started
[npmModule]: https://www.npmjs.com/package/@britecharts/core
[jsDelivrLib]: https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/@britecharts/core/dist/
[jsDelivrDist]: https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/@britecharts/core/dist/cdn/bundle/core.cdn.min.js
[skillsCli]: https://github.com/vercel-labs/skills
[llmsTxt]: https://britecharts.github.io/britecharts/llms.txt
[llmsFullTxt]: https://britecharts.github.io/britecharts/llms-full.txt
[contributing]: https://github.com/britecharts/britecharts/blob/main/.github/CONTRIBUTING.md
[codeOfConduct]: https://github.com/britecharts/britecharts/blob/main/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md

# @britecharts/wrappers

Source: https://britecharts.github.io/britecharts/docs/packages/wrappers-readme

> `@britecharts/wrappers` is a package that simplifies the use of [Britecharts'][britecharts] components with frontend frameworks. 

## Usage
`@britecharts/wrappers` components expose a simple API to allow its use in frontend frameworks. This API contains three methods: `create`, `update`, and `destroy`. 

To use them, you will pass a configuration object following the Britecharts core component API and a container:

```js
import { BarWrapper } from '@britecharts/wrappers';

const container = document.querySelector('.container');
const data = [
    {
        name: 'Vibrant',
        value: 2,
    },
    {
        name: 'Opalescent',
        value: 4,
    },
    {
        name: 'Shining',
        value: 3,
    },
];
const configuration = {
    width: 400,
    margin: {left: 10},
};

const barInstance = BarWrapper.create(container, data, configuration);

//...

BarWrapper.update(container, newData, {}, barInstance);

```

The wrappers include a lightweight configuration and container validation. 

A configuration value of `undefined` or `null` means "not set" and the chart keeps its own default. Any other value is applied, including the falsy ones: `false`, `0` and `''` reach the chart, so a setting can be turned back off with `{ isLoading: false }`.

In theory, you shouldn't be using this wrappers by themselves, but you might prefer this API (more OO-like) for your vanilla JavaScript projects.

## API
The API of the wrappers has only three methods: `create`, `update` and `destroy`. Note that each component wrapper's configuration options is a reflection of [Britecharts][britecharts-api] charts' APIs.

### Create
Creates a new Britechart chart and returns its instance.

Signature:
`<Wrapper>.create(HTMLElement, <ChartDataShape>, <ConfigurationObject>) => BritechartChart`

Example:
```js
const barInstance = BarWrapper.create(container, data, configuration);
```

### Update
Updates a chart with new data or configuration.

Signature:
`<Wrapper>.update(HTMLElement, <ChartDataShape>, <ConfigurationObject>, BritechartChart) => BritechartChart`

Example:
```js
BarWrapper.update(container, newData, {}, barInstance);
```

### Destroy
Removes the chart's `svg` from the container, so the container can be used again (a `create` after a `destroy` draws exactly one chart). It only removes that `svg`: never the container itself, which a framework may own, nor anything else inside it.

Signature:
`<Wrapper>.destroy(HTMLElement) => void`

Example:
```js
BarWrapper.destroy(container);
```

`TooltipWrapper.destroy` has its own contract: it removes the tooltip from inside the element and never an `svg`, because a tooltip is created inside the chart it decorates and destroyed against the element around it.

### Validation
`create` and `update` check the configuration before drawing, and throw an error that says what to fix: a key the chart has no accessor for, with the nearest one it does have, and a value of the wrong type, with the type it should be.

```
Value not supported by Britechart: height chartGradient
  height: expected a number, got the string "300"
  chartGradient: expected an array of 2 strings, got an array of 1
Supported accessors: https://britecharts.github.io/britecharts/docs/API/bar
```

An `undefined` or `null` value is skipped, and the chart keeps its default.

### Chart specs and their JSON Schemas
A chart can be written down as a spec: its name, its configuration and its data. Each chart has a JSON Schema for its spec, generated from the TypeScript types the wrappers take, so editors and coding agents can check a spec, and complete it, without running it:

```json
{
    "$schema": "https://britecharts.github.io/britecharts/schema/v3/bar.json",
    "chart": "bar",
    "config": { "isHorizontal": true, "a11yTitle": "Signups by plan" },
    "data": [{ "name": "Pro", "value": 412 }]
}
```

The schemas are published at `https://britecharts.github.io/britecharts/schema/v3/<chart>.json` and ship in this package as `@britecharts/wrappers/schemas/<chart>.json`, one per chart, named as core names it (`bar`, `groupedBar`, `scatterPlot`…). Draw a spec with its wrapper: `BarWrapper.create(element, spec.data, spec.config)`. Options that take a function, such as the events and the formatting functions, can't be written in JSON; set them from JavaScript.

## Availability
Every chart in `@britecharts/core` has a wrapper: `BarWrapper`, `BrushWrapper`, `BulletWrapper`, `DonutWrapper`, `GroupedBarWrapper`, `HeatmapWrapper`, `LegendWrapper`, `LineWrapper`, `ScatterPlotWrapper`, `SparklineWrapper`, `StackedAreaWrapper` and `StackedBarWrapper`, plus `TooltipWrapper` for the tooltip.

## Installation

To install run:

```
pnpm add @britecharts/core @britecharts/wrappers
```
Or, with npm:

```
npm i --save @britecharts/core @britecharts/wrappers
```

### Roadmap
Our idea for the short term is to update this package to use TypeScript natively. [Let us know][d3Slack] if you want to help with it.

[britecharts]: https://github.com/britecharts/
[britecharts-api]: https://britecharts.github.io/britecharts/docs/Britecharts
[d3Slack]: https://d3js.slack.com/

# @britecharts/react

Source: https://britecharts.github.io/britecharts/docs/packages/react-readme

> `@britecharts/react` is a package that allows you use [Britecharts][britecharts] within [React][react] applications.

## Usage
Every chart in `@britecharts/react` is a function component: you pass in some props, and it renders a chart.

```jsx
import { Bar } from '@britecharts/react';

const data = [
    {
        name: 'Vibrant',
        value: 2,
    },
    {
        name: 'Opalescent',
        value: 4,
    },
    {
        name: 'Shining',
        value: 3,
    },
];

<Bar
    data={data}
    width={400}
    isHorizontal
/>
```

Check our [Storybook][storybook] for more examples and check the source to copy/paste code.

### Loading data

`data` is required. Pass `null` while it loads: nothing is drawn until it arrives, and the chart is drawn as soon as it does. Leaving `data` out, or passing `undefined`, is an error (and a type error, too).

```jsx
<Bar data={isLoading ? null : data} />
```

### Updating a chart

A chart is redrawn when its props change, and only then. On every render the data and each configuration value are compared with what was last drawn, so a re-render with the same props costs nothing. The consequence is that **the data has to be a new array or object to be redrawn**: mutating it in place and re-rendering with the same reference does nothing.

```jsx
setData([...data, newPoint]); // redraws
data.push(newPoint);
setData(data); // does not: same array, nothing changed
```

### No instance, no ref

Function components have no instance to point a `ref` at, so a `ref` on a chart is not accepted (the typings say so). A chart is drawn into a `<div>` the component owns, and removes what it drew when it unmounts.

### Tooltips

A `Tooltip` wraps the chart it decorates: give it a `render` prop that returns the chart, and pass on the props it hands you, which are what connect the two.

The charts name the fields of their data points differently, so some of them need the tooltip told where to look:

| Chart | `Tooltip` props |
| --- | --- |
| `Line` | `topicLabel="topics"` |
| `StackedArea` | none |
| `StackedBar` | `nameLabel="stack"` |
| `GroupedBar` | `nameLabel="group"` |
| `ScatterPlot` | `valueLabel="y"` |
| `Bar`, `Donut`, `Heatmap` | none |

Without them, the tooltip shows no rows (line), rows without their colours (stacked and grouped bar) or no value (scatter plot).

```jsx
import { Line, Tooltip } from '@britecharts/react';

<Tooltip
    data={data}
    render={(props) => <Line {...props} />}
    topicLabel="topics"
    title="A title"
/>
```

### Responsive charts

`ResponsiveContainer` hands its `render` prop the width it has measured, and measures again when the window is resized. `withResponsiveness` does the same for a component you wrap, as its `width` prop (a `width` you pass yourself wins).

```jsx
import { Line, ResponsiveContainer, withResponsiveness } from '@britecharts/react';

<ResponsiveContainer
    render={({ width }) => <Line data={data} width={width} />}
/>

const ResponsiveLine = withResponsiveness(Line);

<ResponsiveLine data={data} />
```

## API
Each component's API is a reflection of [Britecharts][britecharts] charts and their APIs. They also have a bunch of React specific props, and there are some changes due to the declarative way of building with React. 

For example, if we need to check the options of a bar chart, you will first check the [bar chart's API][barChartAPI] in the main project API reference page.

Every Britecharts chart has a component:
- Bar charts [(API)][barChartAPI]
- Brush charts [(API)][brushAPI]
- Bullet charts [(API)][bulletAPI]
- Grouped Bar charts [(API)][groupedBarChartAPI]
- Donut charts [(API)][donutChartAPI]
- Heatmaps [(API)][heatmapAPI]
- Line charts [(API)][lineChartAPI]
- Scatter Plots [(API)][scatterPlotAPI]
- Sparkline charts [(API)][sparklineChartAPI]
- Stacked Area charts [(API)][stackedAreaChartAPI]
- Stacked Bar charts [(API)][stackedBarChartAPI]
- Tooltips [(API)][tooltipAPI], wrapping the line, stacked area, stacked bar and grouped bar charts with a list of values, and the bar, scatter plot and heatmap charts with a single value (the mini tooltip)
- Legends [(API)][legendAPI]
- The `ResponsiveContainer` component and the `withResponsiveness` function, described above

These components were previously hosted in the [britecharts-react][britecharts-react] repository, but became a package with Britecharts V3.

## Installation

To install run:

```
pnpm add @britecharts/core @britecharts/wrappers @britecharts/react
```
Or, with npm:

```
npm i --save @britecharts/core @britecharts/wrappers @britecharts/react
```

Britecharts-React is available as an [NPM module][npmModule] or through CDN links (in [different formats][jsDelivrLib] or a [bundle][jsDelivrDist]).

Import the components from the package: bundlers get ES modules, and `require('@britecharts/react')` gets the UMD bundle. The [React consumer][testProject] in the integration package shows every way of loading it, and is what CI runs.

### Supported React versions

`peerDependencies` requires `react` and `react-dom` `>=16.8`: the components use hooks, which arrived in that release. What is actually verified on every commit:

- **React 19**, by the unit tests, which now run on React Testing Library, and in a real browser: CI packs the package the way a release does, installs it into a React 19 project, and loads it in production and in a development build under `StrictMode`, which runs every effect's setup, cleanup and setup again.

React 17 and 18 are expected to work and are not exercised. If you hit a version-specific problem on an older React, please open an issue.

## Acknowledgments
For this project, we have followed the approach called ‘Mapping Lifecycle methods’ based on [Nicholas Hery's article][integration-article]: a chart's `create`, `update` and `destroy` are called from the component's mount, update and unmount, which one internal hook now does for every chart. We want to recognize all the contributors in the parent project [Britecharts][britecharts].

## See Also
- [Documentation Homepage][homepage]
- [Contributing Guide][contributing]
- [Code of Conduct][codeOfConduct]

## Contribute
When Britecharts adds a chart, check out our [how-to guide for creating new charts][howtoCreate] to bring it to React. Check also the [contributing guide][contributing] if you want to help.

Note that the aim of this project is to allow the usage of Britecharts within your React applications. For that, we are ‘wrapping’ Britecharts with `@britecharts/wrappers`. This means that **any new features need to first be implemented on Britecharts**. Only then you could update the props and logic that passes in the configuration.

### TypeScript
The package is written in TypeScript, and its type declarations are generated from the components at build time. Each component's props type is exported from the package root (`BarChartProps`, `LineProps` and so on), and CI compiles a TypeScript project against the packed package.

# Bar

Source: https://britecharts.github.io/britecharts/docs/API/bar

Bar Chart reusable API class that renders a
simple and configurable bar chart.

**Example**  
```js
import { select } from 'd3-selection';
import { bar } from '@britecharts/core';

// dataset: [{ name, value }]
const barChart = bar();

barChart
    .height(500)
    .width(800);

select('.css-selector')
    .datum(dataset)
    .call(barChart);
```

## exports(_selection, _data)
This function creates the graph using the selection as container

**Kind**: Exported function  

| Param | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| _selection | `D3Selection` | A d3 selection that represents                                  the container(s) where the chart(s) will be rendered |
| _data | `BarChartData` | The data to attach and generate the chart |

## a11yTitle(_x) ⇒ `String` \| `null` \| `module`
Gets or Sets the name screen readers announce for the chart. It is
set as the svg's `aria-label`. Unset, the chart is announced as
"Bar chart".

**Returns**: `String` \| `null` \| `module` - Current a11yTitle or Chart module to chain calls  

| Param | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| _x | `String` \| `null` | Desired accessible title for the chart |

## a11yDescription(_x) ⇒ `String` \| `null` \| `module`
Gets or Sets a longer description screen readers announce after the
chart's name, such as what the data shows. It is rendered as the svg's
`<desc>`. Unset, the chart has no description.

**Returns**: `String` \| `null` \| `module` - Current a11yDescription or Chart module to chain calls  

| Param | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| _x | `String` \| `null` | Desired accessible description for the chart |

## a11yDataTable(_x) ⇒ `Boolean` \| `module`
Gets or Sets whether the chart renders its data as a visually hidden
table after its svg, which screen readers can read cell by cell. On by
default; set it to false when the app gives the data its own accessible
form.

**Returns**: `Boolean` \| `module` - Current a11yDataTable or Chart module to chain calls  

| Param | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| _x | `Boolean` | Whether to render the data table |

## a11yKeyboardNavigation(_x) ⇒ `Boolean` \| `module`
Gets or Sets whether a keyboard can move through the chart's data
points: the chart takes one tab stop, the arrow keys move between
points, Home and End go to the first and last, and Escape lets go. The
tooltip and highlights follow focus as they follow the pointer. On by
default.

**Returns**: `Boolean` \| `module` - Current a11yKeyboardNavigation or Chart module to chain calls  

| Param | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| _x | `Boolean` | Whether the keyboard can move through the data |

## animationDuration(_x) ⇒ `duration` \| `module`
Gets or Sets the duration of the animation

**Returns**: `duration` \| `module` - Current animation duration or Chart module to chain calls  

| Param | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| _x | `Number` | `1200` | Desired animation duration for the graph |

## betweenBarsPadding(_x) ⇒ `padding` \| `module`
Gets or Sets the padding of the chart (Default is 0.1)

**Returns**: `padding` \| `module` - Current padding or Chart module to chain calls  

| Param | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| _x | `Number` \| `module` | Padding value to get/set |

## chartGradient(_x) ⇒ `Array.<String>` \| `module`
Gets or Sets the gradient colors of a bar in the chart

**Returns**: `Array.<String>` \| `module` - Current color gradient or Line Chart module to chain calls  

| Param | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| _x | `Array.<String>` | Desired color gradient for the line (array of two hexadecimal numbers) |

## colorMap([_x]) ⇒ `object` \| `module`
Gets or Sets the colorMap of the chart

**Returns**: `object` \| `module` - Current colorMap or Chart module to chain calls  

| Param | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| [_x] | `object` | `` | Color map |

**Example**  
```js

```

**Returns**: `colorSchema` \| `module` - Current colorSchema or Chart module to chain calls  

| Param | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |

## enableLabels([_x]) ⇒ `Boolean` \| `module`
If true, adds labels at the end of the bars

**Returns**: `Boolean` \| `module` - Current value of enableLabels or Chart module to chain calls  

| Param | Type | Default |
| --- | --- | --- |
| [_x] | `Boolean` | `false` | 

## exportChart(filename, title) ⇒ `Promise`
Exports the chart and fires a download: an svg file when the filename
ends in `.svg`, and a png otherwise

**Returns**: `Promise` - Promise that resolves if the chart image was loaded and downloaded successfully  

| Param | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| filename | `String` | Name of the downloaded file, whose extension picks the format |
| title | `String` | Title to add at the top of the exported picture |

## hasPercentage(_x) ⇒ `boolean` \| `module`
Gets or Sets the hasPercentage status

**Returns**: `boolean` \| `module` - Is percentage used or Chart module to chain calls  

| Param | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| _x | `boolean` | Should use percentage as value format |

## hasSingleBarHighlight(_x) ⇒ `boolean` \| `module`
Gets or Sets the hasSingleBarHighlight status.
If the value is true (default), only the hovered bar is considered to
be highlighted and will be darkened by default. If the value is false,
all the bars but the hovered bar are considered to be highlighted
and will be darkened (by default). To customize the bar highlight or
remove it completely, use highlightBarFunction instead.

**Returns**: `boolean` \| `module` - Is hasSingleBarHighlight used or Chart module to chain calls  

| Param | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| _x | `boolean` | Should highlight the hovered bar |

## height(_x) ⇒ `height` \| `module`
Gets or Sets the height of the chart

**Returns**: `height` \| `module` - Current height or Chart module to chain calls  

| Param | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| _x | `number` | Desired width for the graph |

## highlightBarFunction(_x) ⇒ `highlightBarFunction` \| `module`
Gets or Sets the highlightBarFunction function. The callback passed to
this function returns a bar selection from the bar chart. Use this function
if you want to apply a custom behavior to the highlighted bar on hover.
When hasSingleBarHighlight is true the highlighted bar will be the
one that was hovered by the user. When hasSingleBarHighlight is false
the highlighted bars are all the bars but the hovered one. The default
highlight effect on a bar is darkening the highlighted bar(s) color.

**Returns**: `highlightBarFunction` \| `module` - Is highlightBarFunction used or Chart module to chain calls  

| Param | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| _x | `function` | Desired operation operation on a hovered bar passed through callback |

**Example**  
```js
barChart.highlightBarFunction(bar => bar.attr('fill', 'blue'))
barChart.highlightBarFunction(null) // will disable the default highlight effect
```
## isAnimated(_x) ⇒ `isAnimated` \| `module`
Gets or Sets the isAnimated property of the chart, making it to animate when render.
The chart draws without animation when the reader's system asks for
reduced motion (`prefers-reduced-motion`), whatever this is set to.
By default this is 'false'

**Returns**: `isAnimated` \| `module` - Current isAnimated flag or Chart module  

| Param | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| _x | `Boolean` | Desired animation flag |

## isHorizontal(_x) ⇒ `isHorizontal` \| `module`
Gets or Sets the horizontal direction of the chart

**Returns**: `isHorizontal` \| `module` - If it is horizontal or Chart module to chain calls  

| Param | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| _x | `number` | Desired horizontal direction for the graph |

**Returns**: `number` \| `module` - Current offset or Chart module to chain calls  

| Param | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| [_x] | `number` | `7` | Margin offset from end of bar |

| Param | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |

## tooltip(_x) ⇒ `module` \| `null`
Gets or Sets the tooltip the chart shows: a `tooltip()` or a
`miniTooltip()`, set on this chart only. The chart connects it to its
pointer and keyboard events, draws it in place, and sets the labels its
data points need, unless they were set on the tooltip; it does so now
if the chart has drawn, and again on every draw. Its event handlers go
under the `britechartsTooltip` namespace. Null, or another tooltip,
removes the one it had.

**Returns**: `module` \| `null` - Current tooltip or Chart module to chain calls  
**Throws**:

- `Error` When the tooltip is already set on another chart

| Param | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| _x | `module` \| `null` | The tooltip to show |

**Example**  
```js
bar().tooltip(miniTooltip().title('Uses')).render('#chart', data);
```
## render(target, [data]) ⇒ `module`
Draws the chart into a target: a CSS selector, an element or a d3
selection, as `select(target).datum(data).call(chart)` does. A selector
draws into the first element it matches. Without data, the chart
redraws with the data it last drew there.

**Returns**: `module` - The chart module, to chain calls  
**Throws**:

- `Error` When the target matches no element

| Param | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| target | `String` \| `Element` \| `D3Selection` | Where to draw the chart |
| [data] | `Object` | The data to draw |

**Example**  
```js
bar().width(600).render('#chart', data);
```
## exports~BarChartData : `Array.<Object>`
**Kind**: inner typedef of `exports`  
**Properties**

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| value | `Number` | Value of the group (required) |
| name | `String` | Name of the group (required) |

**Example**  
```js
[
    {
        value: 1,
        name: 'glittering'
    },
    {
        value: 1,
        name: 'luminous'
    }
]
```
## exports~LocaleObject : `Object`
**Kind**: inner typedef of `exports`  
**Properties**

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| decimal | `String` | the decimal point(e.g., ".") |
| thousands | `String` | the group separator(e.g., ",") |
| grouping | `Array.<Number>` | the array of group sizes(e.g., [3]), cycled as needed |
| currency | `Array.<String>` | the currency prefix and suffix(e.g., ["$", ""]) |
| numerals | `Array.<String>` | optional; an array of ten strings to replace the numerals 0 - 9. |
| percent | `String` | optional; the percent sign(defaults to "%") |
| minus | `String` | optional; the minus sign(defaults to hyphen - minus, "-") |
| nan | `String` | optional; the not - a - number value(defaults "NaN") See some standard locale object values [here](https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/d3-format/locale/). |

**Example**  
```js
{
    "decimal": ",",
    "thousands": ".",
    "grouping": [3],
    "currency": ["", "\u00a0€"]
}
```

# Brush

Source: https://britecharts.github.io/britecharts/docs/API/brush

Brush Chart reusable API class that renders a
simple and configurable brush chart.

**Example**  
```js
import { select } from 'd3-selection';
import { brush } from '@britecharts/core';

// dataset: [{ date, value }]
const brushChart = brush();

brushChart
    .height(500)
    .width(800);

select('.css-selector')
    .datum(dataset)
    .call(brushChart);
```

## exports(_selection, _data)
This function creates the graph using the selection as container

**Kind**: Exported function  

| Param | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| _selection | `D3Selection` | A d3 selection that represents                                  the container(s) where the chart(s) will be rendered |
| _data | `BrushChartData` | The data to attach and generate the chart |

## axisTimeCombinations
Exposes the constants to be used to force the x axis to respect a certain granularity
current options: MINUTE_HOUR, HOUR_DAY, DAY_MONTH, MONTH_YEAR

**Kind**: static property of `exports`  
**Example**  
```js
brush.xAxisCustomFormat(brush.axisTimeCombinations.HOUR_DAY)
```
## a11yTitle(_x) ⇒ `String` \| `null` \| `module`
Gets or Sets the name screen readers announce for the chart. It is
set as the svg's `aria-label`. Unset, the chart is announced as
"Brush chart".

**Returns**: `String` \| `null` \| `module` - Current a11yTitle or Chart module to chain calls  

| Param | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| _x | `String` \| `null` | Desired accessible title for the chart |

## a11yDescription(_x) ⇒ `String` \| `null` \| `module`
Gets or Sets a longer description screen readers announce after the
chart's name, such as what the data shows. It is rendered as the svg's
`<desc>`. Unset, the chart has no description.

**Returns**: `String` \| `null` \| `module` - Current a11yDescription or Chart module to chain calls  

| Param | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| _x | `String` \| `null` | Desired accessible description for the chart |

## a11yDataTable(_x) ⇒ `Boolean` \| `module`
Gets or Sets whether the chart renders its data as a visually hidden
table after its svg, which screen readers can read cell by cell. On by
default; set it to false when the app gives the data its own accessible
form.

**Returns**: `Boolean` \| `module` - Current a11yDataTable or Chart module to chain calls  

| Param | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| _x | `Boolean` | Whether to render the data table |

## animationDuration(_x) ⇒ `duration` \| `module`
Gets or Sets the duration of the area animation

**Returns**: `duration` \| `module` - Current animation duration or Chart module to chain calls  

| Param | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| _x | `Number` | `1200` | Desired animation duration for the graph |

## areaCurve([_x]) ⇒ `String` \| `module`
Gets or Sets the area curve of the stacked area.

**Returns**: `String` \| `module` - Current area curve setting or Chart module to chain calls  

| Param | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| [_x] | `String` | `&#x27;basis&#x27;` | Desired curve for the area. Other options are: monotoneX, natural, linear, monotoneY, step, stepAfter, stepBefore, cardinal, and catmullRom. Visit https://github.com/d3/d3-shape#curves for more information. |

**Example**  
```js
brushChart.areaCurve('step')
```

**Returns**: `dateRange` \| `module` - Current dateRange or Chart module to chain calls  

| Param | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| [_x] | `Array.<String>` | `[null, null]` | Desired dateRange for the graph |

| Param | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| [_x] | `Array.<String>` | `colorHelper.colorGradients.greenBlue` | Desired gradient for the graph |

Gets or Sets the height of the chart

**Returns**: `Number` \| `Module` - Current height or Chart module to chain calls  

| Param | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| _x | `Number` | Desired width for the graph |

## isAnimated(_x) ⇒ `Boolean` \| `module`
Gets or Sets the isAnimated property of the chart, making it to animate when render.
The chart draws without animation when the reader's system asks for
reduced motion (`prefers-reduced-motion`), whatever this is set to.

**Returns**: `Boolean` \| `module` - Current isAnimated flag or Chart module  

| Param | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| _x | `Boolean` | = false     Desired animation flag |

## isLoading(flag) ⇒ `boolean` \| `module`

| Param | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| flag | `boolean` | Desired value for the loading state |

## isLocked(_x) ⇒ `Boolean` \| `module`
Gets or Sets the isLocked property of the brush, enforcing the initial brush size set with dateRange

**Returns**: `Boolean` \| `module` - Current isLocked flag or Chart module  

| Param | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| _x | `Boolean` | = false     Whether the brush window is locked, requires a value set with '.dateRange` when true |

## locale(_x) ⇒ `String` \| `Module`
Pass language tag for the tooltip to localize the date.
Feature uses Intl.DateTimeFormat, for compatability and support, refer to
https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/JavaScript/Reference/Global_Objects/DateTimeFormat

**Returns**: `String` \| `Module` - Current locale or module to chain calls  

| Param | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| _x | `String` | Must be a language tag (BCP 47) like 'en-US' or 'fr-FR' |

## margin(_x) ⇒ `Object` \| `Module`

**Returns**: `Object` \| `Module` - Current margin or Chart module to chain calls  

| Param | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| _x | `Object` | Margin object to get/set |

| Param | Type | Description |

| Param | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |

## xAxisCustomFormat(_x) ⇒ `String` \| `Module`
Exposes the ability to force the chart to show a certain x format
It requires a `xAxisFormat` of 'custom' in order to work.

**Returns**: `String` \| `Module` - Current format or module to chain calls  

| Param | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| _x | `String` | Desired format for x axis, one of the d3.js date formats [here](https://github.com/d3/d3-time-format#locale_format) |

## xAxisFormat(_x) ⇒ `String` \| `Module`
Exposes the ability to force the chart to show a certain x axis grouping

**Returns**: `String` \| `Module` - Current format or module to chain calls  

| Param | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| _x | `String` | Desired format, a combination of axisTimeCombinations (MINUTE_HOUR, HOUR_DAY, DAY_MONTH, MONTH_YEAR) Set it to 'custom' to make use of specific formats with xAxisCustomFormat |

**Example**  
```js
brushChart.xAxisCustomFormat(brushChart.axisTimeCombinations.HOUR_DAY)
```
## xTicks([_x]) ⇒ `Number` \| `Module`
Exposes the ability to force the chart to show a certain x ticks. It requires a `xAxisCustomFormat` of 'custom' in order to work.
NOTE: This value needs to be a multiple of 2, 5 or 10. They won't always work as expected, as D3 decides at the end
how many and where the ticks will appear.

**Returns**: `Number` \| `Module` - Current number or ticks or module to chain calls  

| Param | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| [_x] | `Number` | `` | Desired number of x axis ticks (multiple of 2, 5 or 10) |

## roundingTimeInterval([_x]) ⇒ `roundingTimeInterval` \| `Module`
Gets or Sets the rounding time interval of the selection boundary

**Returns**: `roundingTimeInterval` \| `Module` - Current time interval or module to chain calls  
**See**: [https://github.com/d3/d3-time#intervals](https://github.com/d3/d3-time#intervals)  

| Param | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| [_x] | `roundingTimeInterval` | `&#x27;timeDay&#x27;` | Desired time interval for the selection, default 'timeDay'. |

**Example**  
```js
All options are:
timeMillisecond, utcMillisecond, timeSecond, utcSecond, timeMinute, utcMinute, timeHour, utcHour, timeDay, utcDay
timeWeek, utcWeek, timeSunday, utcSunday, timeMonday, utcMonday, timeTuesday, utcTuesday, timeWednesday,
utcWednesday, timeThursday, utcThursday, timeFriday, utcFriday, timeSaturday, utcSaturday, timeMonth, utcMonth,
timeYear and utcYear.
```
## render(target, [data]) ⇒ `module`
Draws the chart into a target: a CSS selector, an element or a d3
selection, as `select(target).datum(data).call(chart)` does. A selector
draws into the first element it matches. Without data, the chart
redraws with the data it last drew there.

**Returns**: `module` - The chart module, to chain calls  
**Throws**:

- `Error` When the target matches no element

| Param | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| target | `String` \| `Element` \| `D3Selection` | Where to draw the chart |
| [data] | `Object` | The data to draw |

**Example**  
```js
brush().width(600).render('#chart', data);
```
## "customBrushStart"
Event indicating when the brush moves

**Kind**: event emitted by `exports`  
**See**: [d3-brush:on(brush)](https://github.com/d3/d3-brush#brush_on)  
## "customBrushEnd"
Event indicating the end of a brush gesture

**Kind**: event emitted by `exports`  
**See**: [d3-brush:on(end)](https://github.com/d3/d3-brush#brush_on)

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| value | `Number` | Value to chart (required) |
| date | `Date` | Date of the value in ISO8601 format (required) |

**Example**  
```js
[
    {
        value: 1,
        date: '2011-01-06T00:00:00Z'
    },
    {
        value: 2,
        date: '2011-01-07T00:00:00Z'
    }
]
```

# Bullet

Source: https://britecharts.github.io/britecharts/docs/API/bullet

Reusable Bullet Chart API class that renders a
simple and configurable Bullet Chart.

**Example**  
```js
import { select } from 'd3-selection';
import { bullet } from '@britecharts/core';

// dataset: one object: { ranges, measures, markers }
const bulletChart = bullet();

bulletChart
    .width(containerWidth);

select('.css-selector')
    .datum(dataset)
    .call(bulletChart);
```

## exports(_selection, _data)
This function creates the graph using the selection as container

**Kind**: Exported function  

| Param | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| _selection | `D3Selection` | A d3 selection that represents                                  the container(s) where the chart(s) will be rendered |
| _data | `BulletChartData` | The data to attach and generate the chart |

## a11yTitle(_x) ⇒ `String` \| `null` \| `module`
Gets or Sets the name screen readers announce for the chart. It is
set as the svg's `aria-label`. Unset, the chart is announced as
"Bullet chart".

**Returns**: `String` \| `null` \| `module` - Current a11yTitle or Chart module to chain calls  

| Param | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| _x | `String` \| `null` | Desired accessible title for the chart |

## a11yDescription(_x) ⇒ `String` \| `null` \| `module`
Gets or Sets a longer description screen readers announce after the
chart's name, such as what the data shows. It is rendered as the svg's
`<desc>`. Unset, the chart has no description.

**Returns**: `String` \| `null` \| `module` - Current a11yDescription or Chart module to chain calls  

| Param | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| _x | `String` \| `null` | Desired accessible description for the chart |

## a11yDataTable(_x) ⇒ `Boolean` \| `module`
Gets or Sets whether the chart renders its data as a visually hidden
table after its svg, which screen readers can read cell by cell. On by
default; set it to false when the app gives the data its own accessible
form.

**Returns**: `Boolean` \| `module` - Current a11yDataTable or Chart module to chain calls  

| Param | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| _x | `Boolean` | Whether to render the data table |

## colorSchema(_x) ⇒ `Array.<String>` \| `module`
Gets or Sets the colorSchema of the chart.
The first color from the array will be applied to range bars (the wider bars).
The second color from the array will be applied to measure bars (the narrow bars) and
the third color will be applied to the marker lines.

**Returns**: `Array.<String>` \| `module` - Current colorSchema or Chart module to chain calls  

| Param | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| _x | `Array.<String>` | Desired colorSchema for the graph |

## exportChart(filename, title) ⇒ `Promise`
Exports the chart and fires a download: an svg file when the filename
ends in `.svg`, and a png otherwise

**Returns**: `Promise` - Promise that resolves if the chart image was loaded and downloaded successfully  

| Param | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| filename | `String` | Name of the downloaded file, whose extension picks the format |
| title | `String` | Title to add at the top of the exported picture |

## isLoading(_flag) ⇒ `boolean` \| `module`
Gets or Sets the loading state of the chart

**Returns**: `boolean` \| `module` - Current loading state flag or Chart module to chain calls  

| Param | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| _flag | `boolean` | Desired value for the loading state |

**Example**  
```js
chart.isLoading(true)
```
## height(_x) ⇒ `Number` \| `module`

**Returns**: `Number` \| `module` - Current height or Chart module to chain calls  

| Param | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| _x | `Number` | Desired height for the chart |

## isReverse(_x) ⇒ `Boolean` \| `module`

the elements will be rendered in reverse order.

**Returns**: `Boolean` \| `module` - Current height or Chart module to chain calls  

| Param | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| _x | `Boolean` | `false` | Desired height for the chart |

| Param | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |

| Param | Type | Description |

## render(target, [data]) ⇒ `module`
Draws the chart into a target: a CSS selector, an element or a d3
selection, as `select(target).datum(data).call(chart)` does. A selector
draws into the first element it matches. Without data, the chart
redraws with the data it last drew there.

**Returns**: `module` - The chart module, to chain calls  
**Throws**:

- `Error` When the target matches no element

| Param | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| target | `String` \| `Element` \| `D3Selection` | Where to draw the chart |
| [data] | `Object` | The data to draw |

**Example**  
```js

```
## exports~BulletChartData : `Object`
**Kind**: inner typedef of `exports`  
**Properties**

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| ranges | `Array.<Number>` | Range that encodes the qualitative measure |
| measures | `Array.<Number>` | Range that encodes the performance measure |
| markers | `Array.<Number>` | Marker lines that encode the comparative measure |

**Example**  
```js
{
     ranges: [130, 160, 250],
     measures: [150, 180],
     markers: [175]
}
```

# Donut

Source: https://britecharts.github.io/britecharts/docs/API/donut

Reusable Donut Chart API class that renders a
simple and configurable donut chart.

**Example**  
```js
import { select } from 'd3-selection';
import { donut } from '@britecharts/core';

// dataset: [{ name, quantity, id }]
const donutChart = donut();

donutChart
    .externalRadius(500)
    .internalRadius(200);

select('.css-selector')
    .datum(dataset)
    .call(donutChart);
```

## exports(_selection, _data)
This function creates the graph using the selection as container

**Kind**: Exported function  

| Param | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| _selection | `D3Selection` | A d3 selection that represents                                  the container(s) where the chart(s) will be rendered |
| _data | `DonutChartData` | The data to attach and generate the chart |

## a11yTitle(_x) ⇒ `String` \| `null` \| `module`
Gets or Sets the name screen readers announce for the chart. It is
set as the svg's `aria-label`. Unset, the chart is announced as
"Donut chart".

**Returns**: `String` \| `null` \| `module` - Current a11yTitle or Chart module to chain calls  

| Param | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| _x | `String` \| `null` | Desired accessible title for the chart |

## a11yDescription(_x) ⇒ `String` \| `null` \| `module`
Gets or Sets a longer description screen readers announce after the
chart's name, such as what the data shows. It is rendered as the svg's
`<desc>`. Unset, the chart has no description.

**Returns**: `String` \| `null` \| `module` - Current a11yDescription or Chart module to chain calls  

| Param | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| _x | `String` \| `null` | Desired accessible description for the chart |

## a11yDataTable(_x) ⇒ `Boolean` \| `module`
Gets or Sets whether the chart renders its data as a visually hidden
table after its svg, which screen readers can read cell by cell. On by
default; set it to false when the app gives the data its own accessible
form.

**Returns**: `Boolean` \| `module` - Current a11yDataTable or Chart module to chain calls  

| Param | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| _x | `Boolean` | Whether to render the data table |

## a11yKeyboardNavigation(_x) ⇒ `Boolean` \| `module`
Gets or Sets whether a keyboard can move through the chart's data
points: the chart takes one tab stop, the arrow keys move between
points, Home and End go to the first and last, and Escape lets go. The
tooltip and highlights follow focus as they follow the pointer. On by
default.

**Returns**: `Boolean` \| `module` - Current a11yKeyboardNavigation or Chart module to chain calls  

| Param | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| _x | `Boolean` | Whether the keyboard can move through the data |

## animationDuration(_x) ⇒ `duration` \| `module`
Gets or Sets the duration of the animation

**Returns**: `duration` \| `module` - Current animation duration or Chart module to chain calls  

| Param | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| _x | `Number` | `1200` | Desired animation duration for the graph |

## centeredTextFunction(_x) ⇒ `function` \| `module`
Gets or Sets the centeredTextFunction of the chart. If function is provided
the format will be changed by the custom function's value format.
The default format function value is "${d.percentage}% ${d.name}".
The callback will provide the data object with id, name, percentage, and quantity.
Also provides the component added by the user in each data entry.

**Returns**: `function` \| `module` - Current centeredTextFunction or Chart module to chain calls  

| Param | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| _x | `function` | Custom function that returns a formatted string |

**Example**  
```js
donutChart.centeredTextFunction(d => `${d.id} ${d.quantity}`)
```
## colorMap([_x]) ⇒ `number` \| `module`
Gets or Sets the colorMap of the chart

**Returns**: `number` \| `module` - Current colorMap or Chart module to chain calls  

| Param | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| [_x] | `object` | `` | Color map |

**Example**  
```js
stackedBar.colorMap({groupName: 'colorHex', groupName2: 'colorString'})
```
## colorSchema(_x) ⇒ `String` \| `module`
Gets or Sets the colorSchema of the chart

**Returns**: `String` \| `module` - Current colorSchema or Chart module to chain calls  

| Param | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| _x | `Array.<String>` | Desired colorSchema for the graph |

## emptyDataConfig(_x) ⇒ `Object` \| `module`
Gets or Sets the emptyDataConfig of the chart. If set and data is empty (quantity
adds up to zero or there are no entries), the chart will render an empty slice
with a given color (light gray by default)

**Returns**: `Object` \| `module` - Current config for when chart data is an empty array  

| Param | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| _x | `Object` | EmptyDataConfig object to get/set |

**Example**  
```js
donutChart.emptyDataConfig({showEmptySlice: true, emptySliceColor: '#000000'})
```
## exportChart(filename, title) ⇒ `Promise`
Exports the chart and fires a download: an svg file when the filename
ends in `.svg`, and a png otherwise

**Returns**: `Promise` - Promise that resolves if the chart image was loaded and downloaded successfully  

| Param | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| filename | `String` | Name of the downloaded file, whose extension picks the format |
| title | `String` | Title to add at the top of the exported picture |

## externalRadius(_x) ⇒ `Number` \| `Module`
Gets or Sets the externalRadius of the chart

**Returns**: `Number` \| `Module` - Current externalRadius or Donut Chart module to chain calls  

| Param | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| _x | `Number` | ExternalRadius number to get/set |

## hasCenterLegend(_x) ⇒ `boolean` \| `Module`
Gets or Sets the hasCenterLegend property of the chart, making it display
legend at the center of the donut.

**Returns**: `boolean` \| `Module` - Current hasCenterLegend flag or Chart module  

| Param | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| _x | `boolean` | If we want to show legent at the center of the donut |

## hasHoverAnimation(_x) ⇒ `boolean` \| `module`
Gets or Sets the hasHoverAnimation property of the chart. By default,
donut chart highlights the hovered slice. This property explicitly
disables this hover behavior.

**Returns**: `boolean` \| `module` - Current hasHoverAnimation flag or Chart module  

| Param | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| _x | `boolean` | Decide whether hover slice animation should be enabled |

## hasFixedHighlightedSlice(_x) ⇒ `boolean` \| `module`
Gets or Sets the hasFixedHighlightedSlice property of the chart, making it to
highlight the selected slice id set with `highlightSliceById` all the time.

**Returns**: `boolean` \| `module` - Current hasFixedHighlightedSlice flag or Chart module  

| Param | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| _x | `boolean` | If we want to make the highlighted slice permanently highlighted |

## hasLastHoverSliceHighlighted(_x) ⇒ `boolean` \| `module`
Gets or sets the hasLastHoverSliceHighlighted property.
If property is true, the last hovered slice will be highlighted
after 'mouseout` event is triggered. The last hovered slice will remain
in highlight state.
Note: if both hasFixedHighlightedSlice and hasLastHoverSliceHighlighted
are true, the latter property will override the former.

**Returns**: `boolean` \| `module` - Current hasLastHoverSliceHighlighted value or Chart module  

| Param | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| _x | `boolean` | Decide whether the last hovered slice should be highlighted |

## height(_x) ⇒ `Number` \| `Module`

**Returns**: `Number` \| `Module` - Current height or Donut Chart module to chain calls  

| Param | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| _x | `Number` | Desired width for the graph |

## highlightSliceById(_x) ⇒ `Number` \| `Module`

**Returns**: `Number` \| `Module` - Current highlighted slice id or Donut Chart module to chain calls  

| Param | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| _x | `Number` | Slice id |

By default this is 'false'

**Returns**: `Boolean` \| `module` - Current isAnimated flag or Chart module  

| Param | Type | Description |

| --- | --- | --- |
| _x | `Object` | Margin object to get/set |

| Param | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| _x | `string` | Desired numberFormat for the chart. See examples [here](https://d3js.org/d3-format) |

Exposes an 'on' method that acts as a bridge with the event dispatcher
We are going to expose this events:
customMouseOver, customMouseMove, customMouseOut and customClick

**Returns**: `module` - Bar Chart

| Param | Type | Description |

| _x | `function` | A custom function that sets logic for ordering |

| Param | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| _x | `Number` | Desired width for the graph |

## render(target, [data]) ⇒ `module`
Draws the chart into a target: a CSS selector, an element or a d3
selection, as `select(target).datum(data).call(chart)` does. A selector
draws into the first element it matches. Without data, the chart
redraws with the data it last drew there.

**Returns**: `module` - The chart module, to chain calls  
**Throws**:

- `Error` When the target matches no element

| Param | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| target | `String` \| `Element` \| `D3Selection` | Where to draw the chart |
| [data] | `Object` | The data to draw |

**Example**  
```js
donut().width(600).render('#chart', data);
```
## exports~DonutChartData : `Array.<Object>`
**Kind**: inner typedef of `exports`  
**Properties**

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| quantity | `Number` | Quantity of the group (required) |
| percentage | `Number` | Percentage of the total (optional) |
| name | `String` | Name of the group (required) |
| id | `Number` | Identifier for the group required for legend feature (optional) |

**Example**  
```js
[
    {
        quantity: 1,
        percentage: 50,
        name: 'glittering',
        id: 1
    },
    {
        quantity: 1,
        percentage: 50,
        name: 'luminous',
        id: 2
    }
]
```

# Grouped Bar

Source: https://britecharts.github.io/britecharts/docs/API/grouped-bar

Grouped Bar Chart reusable API module that allows us
rendering a multi grouped bar and configurable chart.

**Example**  
```js
import { select } from 'd3-selection';
import { groupedBar } from '@britecharts/core';

// dataset: [{ name, group, value }]
const groupedBarChart = groupedBar();

groupedBarChart
    .width(containerWidth);

select('.css-selector')
    .datum(dataset)
    .call(groupedBarChart);
```

## exports(_selection, _data)
This function creates the graph using the selection and data provided

**Kind**: Exported function  

| Param | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| _selection | `D3Selection` | A d3 selection that represents the container(s) where the chart(s) will be rendered |
| _data | `GroupedBarChartData` | The data to attach and generate the chart |

## a11yTitle(_x) ⇒ `String` \| `null` \| `module`
Gets or Sets the name screen readers announce for the chart. It is
set as the svg's `aria-label`. Unset, the chart is announced as
"Grouped bar chart".

**Returns**: `String` \| `null` \| `module` - Current a11yTitle or Chart module to chain calls  

| Param | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| _x | `String` \| `null` | Desired accessible title for the chart |

## a11yDescription(_x) ⇒ `String` \| `null` \| `module`
Gets or Sets a longer description screen readers announce after the
chart's name, such as what the data shows. It is rendered as the svg's
`<desc>`. Unset, the chart has no description.

**Returns**: `String` \| `null` \| `module` - Current a11yDescription or Chart module to chain calls  

| Param | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| _x | `String` \| `null` | Desired accessible description for the chart |

## a11yDataTable(_x) ⇒ `Boolean` \| `module`
Gets or Sets whether the chart renders its data as a visually hidden
table after its svg, which screen readers can read cell by cell. On by
default; set it to false when the app gives the data its own accessible
form.

**Returns**: `Boolean` \| `module` - Current a11yDataTable or Chart module to chain calls  

| Param | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| _x | `Boolean` | Whether to render the data table |

## a11yKeyboardNavigation(_x) ⇒ `Boolean` \| `module`
Gets or Sets whether a keyboard can move through the chart's data
points: the chart takes one tab stop, the arrow keys move between
points, Home and End go to the first and last, and Escape lets go. The
tooltip and highlights follow focus as they follow the pointer. On by
default.

**Returns**: `Boolean` \| `module` - Current a11yKeyboardNavigation or Chart module to chain calls  

| Param | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| _x | `Boolean` | Whether the keyboard can move through the data |

## animationDuration(_x) ⇒ `duration` \| `module`
Gets or Sets the duration of the animation

**Returns**: `duration` \| `module` - Current animation duration or Chart module to chain calls  

| Param | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| _x | `Number` | `1200` | Desired animation duration for the graph |

**Returns**: `Number` \| `module` - Current padding or Chart module to chain calls  

| Param | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| [_x] | `Number` | `0.1` | Padding value to get/set |

| Param | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| [_x] | `Number` | `0.1` | Padding value to get/set |

The method accepts both positive and negative values.
