## tooltip(_x) ⇒ `module` \| `null`
Gets or Sets the tooltip the chart shows: a `tooltip()` or a
`miniTooltip()`, set on this chart only. The chart connects it to its
pointer and keyboard events, draws it in place, and sets the labels its
data points need, unless they were set on the tooltip; it does so now
if the chart has drawn, and again on every draw. Its event handlers go
under the `britechartsTooltip` namespace. Null, or another tooltip,
removes the one it had.

**Returns**: `module` \| `null` - Current tooltip or Chart module to chain calls  
**Throws**:

- `Error` When the tooltip is already set on another chart

| Param | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| _x | `module` \| `null` | The tooltip to show |

**Example**  
```js
groupedBar().tooltip(tooltip().title('Uses')).render('#chart', data);
```
## render(target, [data]) ⇒ `module`
Draws the chart into a target: a CSS selector, an element or a d3
selection, as `select(target).datum(data).call(chart)` does. A selector
draws into the first element it matches. Without data, the chart
redraws with the data it last drew there.

**Returns**: `module` - The chart module, to chain calls  
**Throws**:

- `Error` When the target matches no element

| Param | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| target | `String` \| `Element` \| `D3Selection` | Where to draw the chart |
| [data] | `Object` | The data to draw |

**Example**  
```js
groupedBar().width(600).render('#chart', data);
```
## exports~GroupedBarChartData : `Array.<Object>`
**Kind**: inner typedef of `exports`  
**Properties**

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| name | `String` | Name of the entry |
| group | `String` | group of the entry |
| value | `Number` | Value of the entry |

**Example**  
```js
[
    {
        name: "2011-01",
        group: "Direct",
        value: 0
    }
]
```

# Heatmap

Source: https://britecharts.github.io/britecharts/docs/API/heatmap

Reusable Heatmap API module that renders a
simple and configurable heatmap chart.

**Example**  
```js
import { select } from 'd3-selection';
import { heatmap } from '@britecharts/core';

// dataset: [{ day, hour, value }], day 0-6 and hour 0-23, or indexes into
// yAxisLabels and xAxisLabels
const heatmapChart = heatmap();

heatmapChart
    .width(500);

select('.css-selector')
    .datum(dataset)
    .call(heatmapChart);
```

## exports(_selection)
This function creates the graph using the selection as container

**Kind**: Exported function  

| Param | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| _selection | `D3Selection` | A d3 selection that represents                                  the container(s) where the chart(s) will be rendered |

## a11yTitle(_x) ⇒ `String` \| `null` \| `module`
Gets or Sets the name screen readers announce for the chart. It is
set as the svg's `aria-label`. Unset, the chart is announced as
"Heatmap".

| Param | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| _x | `String` \| `null` | Desired accessible title for the chart |

## xAxisLabels(_x) ⇒ `xAxisLabels` \| `module`

these labels rather than the hours of the day, so together with
`yAxisLabels` the heatmap can show any two sets of categories.

**Returns**: `xAxisLabels` \| `module` - Current xAxisLabels array or Chart module to chain calls

## tooltip(_x) ⇒ `module` \| `null`

## render(target, [data]) ⇒ `module`
Draws the chart into a target: a CSS selector, an element or a d3
selection, as `select(target).datum(data).call(chart)` does. A selector
draws into the first element it matches. Without data, the chart
redraws with the data it last drew there.

**Returns**: `module` - The chart module, to chain calls  
**Throws**:

- `Error` When the target matches no element

| Param | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| target | `String` \| `Element` \| `D3Selection` | Where to draw the chart |
| [data] | `Object` | The data to draw |

**Example**  
```js
heatmap().width(600).render('#chart', data);
```
## exports~HeatmapData : `Array.<Object>`
The data a heatmap takes: one entry per box.

**Kind**: inner typedef of `exports`  
**Properties**

| Name | Type |
| --- | --- |
| day | `Number` | 
| hour | `Number` | 
| value | `Number` | 

**Example**  
```js
[
    {
        day: 0,
        hour: 0,
        value: 7
    },
    {
        day: 0,
        hour: 1,
        value: 10
    }
]
```

# Legend

Source: https://britecharts.github.io/britecharts/docs/API/legend

Legend Component reusable API class that renders a
simple and configurable legend element.

**Example**  
```js
import { select } from 'd3-selection';
import { donut, legend } from '@britecharts/core';

// dataset: [{ id, name, quantity }], the same ids for both
const donutChart = donut();
const legendChart = legend();

donutChart
    .externalRadius(500)
    .internalRadius(200)
    .on('customMouseOver', (data) => legendChart.highlight(data.data.id))
    .on('customMouseOut', () => legendChart.clearHighlight());

select('.css-selector')
    .datum(dataset)
    .call(donutChart);

select('.other-css-selector')
    .datum(dataset)
    .call(legendChart);
```

## exports(_selection, _data)
This function creates the graph using the selection as container

**Kind**: Exported function  

| Param | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| _selection | `D3Selection` | A d3 selection that represents                                  the container(s) where the chart(s) will be rendered |
| _data | `LegendChartData` | The data to attach and generate the chart |

## a11yTitle(_x) ⇒ `String` \| `null` \| `module`
Gets or Sets the name screen readers announce for the chart. It is
set as the svg's `aria-label`. Unset, the chart is announced as
"Legend".

**Returns**: `String` \| `null` \| `module` - Current a11yTitle or Chart module to chain calls  

| Param | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| _x | `String` \| `null` | Desired accessible title for the chart |

## a11yDescription(_x) ⇒ `String` \| `null` \| `module`
Gets or Sets a longer description screen readers announce after the
chart's name, such as what the data shows. It is rendered as the svg's
`<desc>`. Unset, the chart has no description.

**Returns**: `String` \| `null` \| `module` - Current a11yDescription or Chart module to chain calls  

| Param | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| _x | `String` \| `null` | Desired accessible description for the chart |

Command that clears all highlighted entries on a legend instance

| Param | Type | Default | Description |

Used to determine spacing between legend elements.

**Returns**: `number` \| `module` - Current marginRatio or Legend module to chain calls  

| Param | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| [_x] | `number` | `1.5` | Margin Ratio to get/set |

## markerSize([_x]) ⇒ `object` \| `module`
Gets or Sets the markerSize of the legend chart.
This markerSize will determine the horizontal and vertical size of the colored marks
added as color identifiers for the chart's categories.

**Returns**: `object` \| `module` - Current markerSize or Legend module to chain calls  

| Param | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| [_x] | `object` | `16` | Margin object to get/set |

## numberFormat(_x) ⇒ `string` \| `module`

| Param | Type | Description |

| Param | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| [_x] | `number` | `320` | Desired width for the graph in pixels |

## render(target, [data]) ⇒ `module`
Draws the chart into a target: a CSS selector, an element or a d3
selection, as `select(target).datum(data).call(chart)` does. A selector
draws into the first element it matches. Without data, the chart
redraws with the data it last drew there.

**Returns**: `module` - The chart module, to chain calls  
**Throws**:

- `Error` When the target matches no element

| Param | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| target | `String` \| `Element` \| `D3Selection` | Where to draw the chart |
| [data] | `Object` | The data to draw |

**Example**  
```js
legend().width(600).render('#chart', data);
```
## exports~LegendChartData : `Array.<Object>`
**Kind**: inner typedef of `exports`  
**Properties**

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| id | `Number` | Id of the group (required) |
| name | `String` | Name of the group (required) |
| quantity | `Number` | Quantity of the group (optional) |

**Example**  
```js
[
    {
        id: 1,
        quantity: 2,
        name: 'glittering'
    },
    {
        id: 2,
        quantity: 3,
        name: 'luminous'
    }
]
```

# Line

Source: https://britecharts.github.io/britecharts/docs/API/line

Line Chart reusable API module that allows us
rendering a multi line and configurable chart.

**Example**  
```js
import { select } from 'd3-selection';
import { line } from '@britecharts/core';

// dataset: { data: [{ topicName, name, date, value }] }
const lineChart = line();

lineChart
    .width(500);

select('.css-selector')
    .datum(dataset)
    .call(lineChart);
```

## exports(_selection, _data)
This function creates the graph using the selection and data provided

**Kind**: Exported function  

| Param | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| _selection | `D3Selection` | A d3 selection that represents                                  the container(s) where the chart(s) will be rendered |
| _data | `LineChartData` | The data to attach and generate the chart |

## axisTimeCombinations
Exposes the constants to be used to force the x axis to respect a certain granularity
current options: MINUTE_HOUR, HOUR_DAY, DAY_MONTH, MONTH_YEAR

**Kind**: static property of `exports`  
**Example**  
```js
line.xAxisFormat(line.axisTimeCombinations.HOUR_DAY)
```
## a11yTitle(_x) ⇒ `String` \| `null` \| `module`
Gets or Sets the name screen readers announce for the chart. It is
set as the svg's `aria-label`. Unset, the chart is announced as
"Line chart".

**Returns**: `String` \| `null` \| `module` - Current a11yTitle or Chart module to chain calls  

| Param | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| _x | `String` \| `null` | Desired accessible title for the chart |

default; set it to false when the app gives the data its own accessible
form.

**Returns**: `Boolean` \| `module` - Current a11yDataTable or Chart module to chain calls  

| Param | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |

## a11yKeyboardNavigation(_x) ⇒ `Boolean` \| `module`
Gets or Sets whether a keyboard can move through the chart's data
points: the chart takes one tab stop, the arrow keys move between
points, Home and End go to the first and last, and Escape lets go. The
tooltip and highlights follow focus as they follow the pointer. On by
default.

**Returns**: `Boolean` \| `module` - Current a11yKeyboardNavigation or Chart module to chain calls  

| Param | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| _x | `Boolean` | Whether the keyboard can move through the data |

## xAxisCustomFormat(_x) ⇒ `string` \| `module`

NOTE: localization not supported

**Returns**: `string` \| `module` - Current format or module to chain calls  

| Param | Type | Description |

Exposes the ability to force the chart to show a certain x axis grouping

**Returns**: `String` \| `Module` - Current format or module to chain calls  

| Param | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| _x | `string` | Desired format, a combination of axisTimeCombinations (MINUTE_HOUR, HOUR_DAY, DAY_MONTH, MONTH_YEAR) Set it to 'custom' to make use of specific formats with xAxisCustomFormat |

**Example**  
```js
line.xAxisCustomFormat(line.axisTimeCombinations.HOUR_DAY)
```
## xTicks(_x) ⇒ `Number` \| `module`
Exposes the ability to force the chart to show a certain x ticks. It requires a `xAxisFormat` of 'custom' in order to work.
NOTE: This value needs to be a multiple of 2, 5 or 10. They won't always work as expected, as D3 decides at the end
how many and where the ticks will appear.

**Returns**: `Number` \| `module` - Current number or ticks or module to chain calls  

| Param | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| _x | `number` | Desired number of x axis ticks (multiple of 2, 5 or 10) |

```js
}])
```

## exportChart(filename, title) ⇒ `Promise`
Exports the chart and fires a download: an svg file when the filename
ends in `.svg`, and a png otherwise

**Returns**: `Promise` - Promise that resolves if the chart image was loaded and downloaded successfully  

| Param | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| filename | `string` | Name of the downloaded file, whose extension picks the format |
| title | `string` | Title to add at the top of the exported picture |

## on() ⇒ `module`
Exposes an 'on' method that acts as a bridge with the event dispatcher
We are going to expose this events:
customMouseHover, customMouseMove, customMouseOut,
customDataEntryClick, and customTouchMove

**Returns**: `module` - Bar Chart  
## xAxisValueType([_x]) ⇒ `string` \| `module`
Gets or Sets the `xAxisValueType`.
Choose between 'date' and 'number'. When set to `number` the values of the x-axis must not
be dates anymore, but can be arbitrary numbers.

**Returns**: `string` \| `module` - Current value type of the x-axis or Chart module to chain calls  

| Param | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| [_x] | `string` | `"&#x27;date&#x27;"` | Desired value type of the x-axis |

**Example**  
```js
line.xAxisValueType('number')
```
## xAxisScale([_x]) ⇒ `string` \| `module`
Gets or Sets the `xAxisScale`.
Choose between 'linear' and 'logarithmic'. The setting will only work if `xAxisValueType` is set to
'number' as well, otherwise it won't influence the visualization.

**Returns**: `string` \| `module` - Current value type of the x-axis or Chart module to chain calls  

| Param | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| [_x] | `string` | `"&#x27;linear&#x27;"` | Desired value type of the x-axis |

**Example**  
```js
line.xAxisValueType('number').xAxisScale('logarithmic')
```
## tooltip(_x) ⇒ `module` \| `null`
Gets or Sets the tooltip the chart shows: a `tooltip()` or a
`miniTooltip()`, set on this chart only. The chart connects it to its
pointer and keyboard events, draws it in place, and sets the labels its
data points need, unless they were set on the tooltip; it does so now
if the chart has drawn, and again on every draw. Its event handlers go
under the `britechartsTooltip` namespace. Null, or another tooltip,
removes the one it had.

**Returns**: `module` \| `null` - Current tooltip or Chart module to chain calls  
**Throws**:

- `Error` When the tooltip is already set on another chart

| Param | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| _x | `module` \| `null` | The tooltip to show |

**Example**  
```js
line().tooltip(tooltip().title('Uses')).render('#chart', data);
```
## render(target, [data]) ⇒ `module`
Draws the chart into a target: a CSS selector, an element or a d3
selection, as `select(target).datum(data).call(chart)` does. A selector
draws into the first element it matches. Without data, the chart
redraws with the data it last drew there.

**Returns**: `module` - The chart module, to chain calls  
**Throws**:

- `Error` When the target matches no element

| Param | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| target | `String` \| `Element` \| `D3Selection` | Where to draw the chart |
| [data] | `Object` | The data to draw |

**Example**  
```js
line().width(600).render('#chart', data);
```
## exports~D3Selection : `Array.<Array>`
**Kind**: inner typedef of `exports`  
**Properties**

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| length | `number` | Size of the selection |
| parentNode | `DOMElement` | Parent of the selection |

## exports~LineChartFlatData : `object`
**Kind**: inner typedef of `exports`  
**Properties**

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| topicName | `string` | Topic name (required) |
| topic | `number` | Topic identifier (required) |
| dates | `Array.<object>` | All date entries with values for that topic in ISO8601 format (required) |

**Example**  
```js
[
    {
        topicName: 'San Francisco',
        name: 123,
        date: '2017-01-16T16:00:00-08:00',
        value: 1
    }
]
```
## exports~LineChartDataSorted : `Array.<object>`
The Data Sorted is calculated internally in the chart in order to pass it to our tooltips

**Kind**: inner typedef of `exports`  
**Properties**

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| date | `string` | | number        Date in ISO8601 format or number (required)] |
| topics | `Array.<object>` | List of topics with values that date (required) |

**Example**  
```js
[
    {
        date: "2015-06-27T07:00:00.000Z",
        topics: [
            {
                "name": 1,
                "value": 1,
                "topicName": "San Francisco"
            },
            {
                "name": 2,
                "value": 20,
                "topicName": "Los Angeles"
            },
            {
                "name": 3,
                "value": 10,
                "topicName": "Oakland"
            }
        ]
    },
    {...}
]
```
## exports~LineChartData : `object`
The data shape for the line chart.
Up to version 2.10.1 this required a "dataByTopic" array. That shape was
removed in 3.0.0 -- pass the flat dataset described here instead.

**Kind**: inner typedef of `exports`  
**Properties**

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| data | `Array.<LineChartFlatData>` | Data values to chart (required) |

**Example**  
```js
{
    data: [
        {
            topicName: 'San Francisco',
            name: 1,
            date: '2017-01-16T16:00:00-08:00',
            value: 1
        },
        {
            topicName: 'San Francisco',
            name: 1,
            date: '2017-01-17T16:00:00-08:00',
            value: 2
        },
        {
            topicName: 'Oakland',
            name: 2,
            date: '2017-01-16T16:00:00-08:00',
            value: 3
        },
        {
            topicName: 'Oakland',
            name: 2,
            date: '2017-01-17T16:00:00-08:00',
            value: 7
        }
    ]
}
```

# Scatter Plot

Source: https://britecharts.github.io/britecharts/docs/API/scatter-plot

Reusable Scatter Plot API class that renders a
simple and configurable scatter chart.

**Example**  
```js
import { select } from 'd3-selection';
import { scatterPlot } from '@britecharts/core';

// dataset: [{ name, x, y }]
const scatterPlotChart = scatterPlot();

scatterPlotChart
    .grid('horizontal')
    .width(500);

select('.css-selector')
    .datum(dataset)
    .call(scatterPlotChart);
```

## exports(_selection, _data)
This function creates the graph using the selection as container

**Kind**: Exported function  

| Param | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| _selection | `D3Selection` | A d3 selection that represents                                  the container(s) where the chart(s) will be rendered |
| _data | `ScatterPlotData` | The data to attach and generate the chart |

## a11yTitle(_x) ⇒ `String` \| `null` \| `module`
Gets or Sets the name screen readers announce for the chart. It is
set as the svg's `aria-label`. Unset, the chart is announced as
"Scatter plot".

**Returns**: `String` \| `null` \| `module` - Current a11yTitle or Chart module to chain calls  

| Param | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| _x | `String` \| `null` | Desired accessible title for the chart |

## a11yDescription(_x) ⇒ `String` \| `null` \| `module`
Gets or Sets a longer description screen readers announce after the
chart's name, such as what the data shows. It is rendered as the svg's
`<desc>`. Unset, the chart has no description.

**Returns**: `String` \| `null` \| `module` - Current a11yDescription or Chart module to chain calls  

| Param | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| _x | `String` \| `null` | Desired accessible description for the chart |

## a11yDataTable(_x) ⇒ `Boolean` \| `module`
Gets or Sets whether the chart renders its data as a visually hidden
table after its svg, which screen readers can read cell by cell. On by
default; set it to false when the app gives the data its own accessible
form.

**Returns**: `Boolean` \| `module` - Current a11yDataTable or Chart module to chain calls  

| Param | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| _x | `Boolean` | Whether to render the data table |

## a11yKeyboardNavigation(_x) ⇒ `Boolean` \| `module`
Gets or Sets whether a keyboard can move through the chart's data
points: the chart takes one tab stop, the arrow keys move between
points, Home and End go to the first and last, and Escape lets go. The
tooltip and highlights follow focus as they follow the pointer. On by
default.

**Returns**: `Boolean` \| `module` - Current a11yKeyboardNavigation or Chart module to chain calls  

| Param | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| _x | `Boolean` | Whether the keyboard can move through the data |

## animationDuration(_x) ⇒ `duration` \| `module`
Gets or Sets the duration of the circle animation

**Returns**: `duration` \| `module` - Current animation duration or Chart module to chain calls  

| Param | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| _x | `Number` | `1200` | Desired animation duration for the graph |

## circleStrokeOpacity(_x) ⇒ `Number` \| `module`
Gets or Sets each circle's border opacity value of the chart.
It makes each circle border transparent if it's less than 1.

**Returns**: `Number` \| `module` - Current circleStrokeOpacity or Chart module to chain calls  

| Param | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| _x | `Number` | `1` | Desired border opacity of circles of the chart |

**Example**  
```js
scatterPlot.circleStrokeOpacity(0.6)
```
## circleStrokeWidth(_x) ⇒ `Number` \| `module`
Gets or Sets each circle's border width value of the chart.
It makes each circle border transparent if it's less than 1.

**Returns**: `Number` \| `module` - Current circleStrokeWidth or Chart module to chain calls  

| Param | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| _x | `Number` | `1` | Desired border width of circles of the chart |

**Example**  
```js
scatterPlot.circleStrokeWidth(10)
```
## circleOpacity(_x) ⇒ `Number` \| `module`
Gets or Sets the circles opacity value of the chart.
Use this to set opacity of a circle for each data point of the chart.
It makes the area of each data point more transparent if it's less than 1.

**Returns**: `Number` \| `module` - Current circleOpacity or Chart module to chain calls  

| Param | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| _x | `Number` | `0.24` | Desired opacity of circles of the chart |

**Example**  
```js
scatterPlot.circleOpacity(0.6)
```
## colorMap([_x]) ⇒ `object` \| `module`

**Returns**: `object` \| `module` - Current colorMap or Chart module to chain calls  

| Param | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| [_x] | `object` | `` | Color map |

## exportChart(filename, title) ⇒ `Promise`

**Returns**: `Promise` - Promise that resolves if the chart image was loaded and downloaded successfully  

| Param | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| filename | `String` | Name of the downloaded file, whose extension picks the format |
| title | `String` | Title to add at the top of the exported picture |

## grid(_x) ⇒ `String` \| `module`

**Returns**: `String` \| `module` - Current mode of the grid or Chart module to chain calls  

| Param | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| _x | `String` | Desired mode for the grid ('vertical'|'horizontal'|'full') |

## hasCrossHairs(_x) ⇒ `boolean` \| `module`
Gets or Sets the hasCrossHairs status. If true,
the hovered data point will be highlighted with lines
and legend from both x and y axis. The user will see
values for x under x axis line and y under y axis. Lines
will be drawn with respect to highlighted data point

**Returns**: `boolean` \| `module` - Current hasCrossHairs or Chart module to chain calls  

| Param | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| _x | `boolean` | `false` | Desired hasCrossHairs status for chart |

## hasHollowCircles(_x) ⇒ `boolean` \| `module`

| Param | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| _x | `boolean` | `false` | Choose whether chart's data points/circles should be hollow |

## hasTrendline(_x) ⇒ `boolean` \| `module`

If true, the trendline calculated based off linear regression
formula will be drawn

**Returns**: `boolean` \| `module` - Current hasTrendline value or Chart module to chain calls  

| Param | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |

## tooltip(_x) ⇒ `module` \| `null`
Gets or Sets the tooltip the chart shows: a `tooltip()` or a
`miniTooltip()`, set on this chart only. The chart connects it to its
pointer and keyboard events, draws it in place, and sets the labels its
data points need, unless they were set on the tooltip; it does so now
if the chart has drawn, and again on every draw. Its event handlers go
under the `britechartsTooltip` namespace. Null, or another tooltip,
removes the one it had.

**Returns**: `module` \| `null` - Current tooltip or Chart module to chain calls  
**Throws**:

- `Error` When the tooltip is already set on another chart

| Param | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| _x | `module` \| `null` | The tooltip to show |

**Example**  
```js
scatterPlot().tooltip(miniTooltip()).render('#chart', data);
```
## render(target, [data]) ⇒ `module`
Draws the chart into a target: a CSS selector, an element or a d3
selection, as `select(target).datum(data).call(chart)` does. A selector
draws into the first element it matches. Without data, the chart
redraws with the data it last drew there.

**Returns**: `module` - The chart module, to chain calls  
**Throws**:

- `Error` When the target matches no element

| Param | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| target | `String` \| `Element` \| `D3Selection` | Where to draw the chart |
| [data] | `Object` | The data to draw |

**Example**  
```js
scatterPlot().width(600).render('#chart', data);
```
## exports~nameToColorMap
Maps data point category name to
each color of the given color scheme
{
    name1: 'color1',
    name2: 'color2',
    name3: 'color3',
    ...
}

**Kind**: inner property of `exports`  
## exports~ScatterPlotData : `Array.<Object>`
**Kind**: inner typedef of `exports`  
**Properties**

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| name | `String` | Name of the category or topic for data point |
| x | `Number` | Data point's position value relative to x-axis |
| y | `Number` | Data point's position value relative to y-axis |

**Example**  
```js
[
    {
        name: 'topic',
        x: 123,
        y: 24,
    },
    {
        name: 'topic1',
        x: 53,
        y: 31,
    },
    {
        name: 'topic2',
        x: 631,
        y: 321,
    },
    {
        name: 'topic1',
        x: 231,
        y: 111,
    }
]
```

# Sparkline

Source: https://britecharts.github.io/britecharts/docs/API/sparkline

Sparkline Chart reusable API module that allows us
rendering a sparkline configurable chart.

**Example**  
```js
import { select } from 'd3-selection';
import { sparkline } from '@britecharts/core';

// dataset: [{ date, value }]
const sparklineChart = sparkline();

sparklineChart
    .width(200)
    .height(100);

select('.css-selector')
    .datum(dataset)
    .call(sparklineChart);
```

## exports(_selection, _data)
This function creates the graph using the selection and data provided

**Kind**: Exported function  

| Param | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| _selection | `D3Selection` | A d3 selection that represents the container(s) where the chart(s) will be rendered |
| _data | `SparklineChartData` | The data to attach and generate the chart |

# Stacked Area

Source: https://britecharts.github.io/britecharts/docs/API/stacked-area

Stacked Area Chart reusable API module that allows us
rendering a multi area and configurable chart.

**Example**  
```js
import { select } from 'd3-selection';
import { stackedArea } from '@britecharts/core';

// dataset: [{ date, name, value }]
const stackedAreaChart = stackedArea();

stackedAreaChart
    .width(containerWidth);

select('.css-selector')
    .datum(dataset)
    .call(stackedAreaChart);
```

## exports(_selection, _data)
This function creates the graph using the selection and data provided

**Kind**: Exported function  

| Param | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| _selection | `D3Selection` | A d3 selection that represents the container(s) where the chart(s) will be rendered |
| _data | `AreaChartData` | The data to attach and generate the chart |

## axisTimeCombinations
Exposes the constants to be used to force the x axis to respect a certain granularity
current options: MINUTE_HOUR, HOUR_DAY, DAY_MONTH, MONTH_YEAR

**Kind**: static property of `exports`  
**Example**  
```js
area.xAxisCustomFormat(area.axisTimeCombinations.HOUR_DAY)
```

| Param | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| _x | `String` \| `null` | Desired accessible title for the chart |

## a11yDescription(_x) ⇒ `String` \| `null` \| `module`

| Param | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |

## a11yDataTable(_x) ⇒ `Boolean` \| `module`
Gets or Sets whether the chart renders its data as a visually hidden
table after its svg, which screen readers can read cell by cell. On by
default; set it to false when the app gives the data its own accessible
form.

**Returns**: `Boolean` \| `module` - Current a11yDataTable or Chart module to chain calls  

| Param | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| _x | `Boolean` | Whether to render the data table |

## a11yKeyboardNavigation(_x) ⇒ `Boolean` \| `module`
Gets or Sets whether a keyboard can move through the chart's data
points: the chart takes one tab stop, the arrow keys move between
points, Home and End go to the first and last, and Escape lets go. The
tooltip and highlights follow focus as they follow the pointer. On by
default.

**Returns**: `Boolean` \| `module` - Current a11yKeyboardNavigation or Chart module to chain calls  

| Param | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| _x | `Boolean` | Whether the keyboard can move through the data |

| Param | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| _x | `Number` | `1200` | Desired animation duration for the graph |

## areaCurve([_x]) ⇒ `String` \| `module`
Gets or Sets the area curve of the stacked area.

**Returns**: `String` \| `module` - Current area curve setting or Chart module to chain calls  

| Param | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| [_x] | `String` | `&#x27;monotoneX&#x27;` | Desired curve for the stacked area, default 'monotoneX'. Other options are: basis, natural, linear, monotoneY, step, stepAfter, stepBefore, cardinal, and catmullRom. Visit https://github.com/d3/d3-shape#curves for more information. |

**Example**  
```js
stackedArea.areaCurve('step')
```

Meant for data without negative values.

**Returns**: `Boolean` \| `module` - If it is normalized or Chart module to chain calls  

| Param | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| _x | `Boolean` | = false     Whether to stack to 100% |

**Example**  
```js

```

## xAxisCustomFormat(_x) ⇒ `String` \| `Module`
Exposes the ability to force the chart to show a certain x format
It requires a `xAxisFormat` of 'custom' in order to work.
NOTE: localization not supported

**Returns**: `String` \| `Module` - Current format or module to chain calls  

| Param | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| _x | `String` | Desired format for x axis, one of the d3.js date formats [here](https://github.com/d3/d3-time-format#locale_format) |

**Example**  
```js
stackedArea.xAxisCustomFormat(stackedArea.axisTimeCombinations.HOUR_DAY)
```
## xAxisFormat(_x) ⇒ `String` \| `Module`
Exposes the ability to force the chart to show a certain x axis grouping

**Returns**: `String` \| `Module` - Current format or module to chain calls  

| Param | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| _x | `String` | Desired format, a combination of axisTimeCombinations (MINUTE_HOUR, HOUR_DAY, DAY_MONTH, MONTH_YEAR) Set it to 'custom' to make use of specific formats with xAxisCustomFormat |

**Example**  
```js
stackedArea.xAxisCustomFormat(stackedArea.axisTimeCombinations.HOUR_DAY)
```
## xAxisValueType([_x]) ⇒ `string` \| `module`
Gets or Sets the `xAxisValueType`.
Choose between 'date' and 'number'. When set to `number` the values of the x-axis must not
be dates anymore, but can be arbitrary numbers.

**Returns**: `string` \| `module` - Current value type of the x-axis or Chart module to chain calls  

| Param | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| [_x] | `string` | `"&#x27;date&#x27;"` | Desired value type of the x-axis |

**Example**  
```js
stackedArea.xAxisValueType('number')
```
## xAxisScale([_x]) ⇒ `string` \| `module`
Gets or Sets the `xAxisScale`.
Choose between 'linear' and 'logarithmic'. The setting will only work if `xAxisValueType` is set to
'number' as well, otherwise it won't influence the visualization.

**Returns**: `string` \| `module` - Current value type of the x-axis or Chart module to chain calls  

| Param | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| [_x] | `string` | `"&#x27;linear&#x27;"` | Desired value type of the x-axis |

**Example**  
```js
stackedArea.xAxisValueType('number').xAxisScale('logarithmic')
```
## xTicks(_x) ⇒ `Number` \| `Module`
Exposes the ability to force the chart to show a certain x ticks. It requires a `xAxisFormat` of 'custom' in order to work.
NOTE: This value needs to be a multiple of 2, 5 or 10. They won't always work as expected, as D3 decides at the end
how many and where the ticks will appear.

**Returns**: `Number` \| `Module` - Current number or ticks or module to chain calls  

| Param | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| _x | `Number` | Desired number of x axis ticks (multiple of 2, 5 or 10) |

## yAxisLabel(_x) ⇒ `String` \| `module`
Gets or Sets the y-axis label of the chart

**Returns**: `String` \| `module` - Current yAxisLabel or Chart module to chain calls  

| Param | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| _x | `String` | Desired label string |

**Example**  
```js
stackedArea.yAxisLabel('Ticket Sales')
```
## yAxisLabelOffset([_x]) ⇒ `Number` \| `module`
Gets or Sets the offset of the yAxisLabel of the chart.
The method accepts both positive and negative values.

**Returns**: `Number` \| `module` - Current yAxisLabelOffset or Chart module to chain calls  

| Param | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| [_x] | `Number` | `-60` | Desired offset for the label |


| Param | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| [_x] | `Number` | `5` | Desired vertical ticks |

## yAxisBaseline([_x]) ⇒ `Number` \| `module`
Gets or Sets the yAxisBaseline - this is the y-value where the area starts from in y-direction
(default is 0). Change this value if you don't want to start your area from y=0.

**Returns**: `Number` \| `module` - Current baseline or Chart module to chain calls  

| Param | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| [_x] | `Number` | `0` | Desired baseline of the y axis |

**Example**  
```js
stackedArea.yAxisBaseline(20)
```
## tooltip(_x) ⇒ `module` \| `null`
Gets or Sets the tooltip the chart shows: a `tooltip()` or a
`miniTooltip()`, set on this chart only. The chart connects it to its
pointer and keyboard events, draws it in place, and sets the labels its
data points need, unless they were set on the tooltip; it does so now
if the chart has drawn, and again on every draw. Its event handlers go
under the `britechartsTooltip` namespace. Null, or another tooltip,
removes the one it had.

**Returns**: `module` \| `null` - Current tooltip or Chart module to chain calls  
**Throws**:

- `Error` When the tooltip is already set on another chart

| Param | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| _x | `module` \| `null` | The tooltip to show |

**Example**  
```js
stackedArea().tooltip(tooltip().title('Uses')).render('#chart', data);
```
## render(target, [data]) ⇒ `module`
Draws the chart into a target: a CSS selector, an element or a d3
selection, as `select(target).datum(data).call(chart)` does. A selector
draws into the first element it matches. Without data, the chart
redraws with the data it last drew there.

**Returns**: `module` - The chart module, to chain calls  
**Throws**:

- `Error` When the target matches no element

| Param | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| target | `String` \| `Element` \| `D3Selection` | Where to draw the chart |
| [data] | `Object` | The data to draw |

**Example**  
```js
stackedArea().width(600).render('#chart', data);
```
## exports~AreaChartData : `Array.<Object>`
**Kind**: inner typedef of `exports`  
**Properties**

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| date | `String` | Date of the entry in ISO8601 format (required) |
| name | `String` | Name of the entry (required) |
| value | `Number` | Value of the entry (required) |

**Example**  
```js
[
    {
        date: "2011-01-05T00:00:00Z",
        name: "Direct",
        value: 0
    }
]
```

---

# Stacked Bar

Source: https://britecharts.github.io/britecharts/docs/API/stacked-bar

Stacked Bar Chart reusable API module that allows us
rendering a multi stacked bar and configurable chart.

**Example**  
```js
import { select } from 'd3-selection';
import { stackedBar } from '@britecharts/core';

// dataset: [{ name, stack, value }]
const stackedBarChart = stackedBar();

stackedBarChart
    .width(containerWidth);

select('.css-selector')
    .datum(dataset)
    .call(stackedBarChart);
```

## exports(_selection, _data)
This function creates the graph using the selection and data provided

**Kind**: Exported function  

| Param | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| _selection | `D3Selection` | A d3 selection that represents the container(s) where the chart(s) will be rendered |
| _data | `StackedBarData` | The data to attach and generate the chart |

## a11yTitle(_x) ⇒ `String` \| `null` \| `module`
Gets or Sets the name screen readers announce for the chart. It is
set as the svg's `aria-label`. Unset, the chart is announced as
"Stacked bar chart".

**Returns**: `String` \| `null` \| `module` - Current a11yTitle or Chart module to chain calls  

| Param | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| _x | `String` \| `null` | Desired accessible title for the chart |

## a11yDescription(_x) ⇒ `String` \| `null` \| `module`
Gets or Sets a longer description screen readers announce after the
chart's name, such as what the data shows. It is rendered as the svg's
`<desc>`. Unset, the chart has no description.

**Returns**: `String` \| `null` \| `module` - Current a11yDescription or Chart module to chain calls  

| Param | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| _x | `String` \| `null` | Desired accessible description for the chart |

| Param | Type | Description |

`miniTooltip()`, set on this chart only. The chart connects it to its
pointer and keyboard events, draws it in place, and sets the labels its
data points need, unless they were set on the tooltip; it does so now
if the chart has drawn, and again on every draw. Its event handlers go
under the `britechartsTooltip` namespace. Null, or another tooltip,
removes the one it had.

**Returns**: `module` \| `null` - Current tooltip or Chart module to chain calls  
**Throws**:

- `Error` When the tooltip is already set on another chart

| Param | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| _x | `module` \| `null` | The tooltip to show |

**Example**  
```js
stackedBar().tooltip(tooltip().title('Uses')).render('#chart', data);
```
## render(target, [data]) ⇒ `module`
Draws the chart into a target: a CSS selector, an element or a d3
selection, as `select(target).datum(data).call(chart)` does. A selector
draws into the first element it matches. Without data, the chart
redraws with the data it last drew there.

**Returns**: `module` - The chart module, to chain calls  
**Throws**:

- `Error` When the target matches no element

| Param | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| target | `String` \| `Element` \| `D3Selection` | Where to draw the chart |
| [data] | `Object` | The data to draw |

**Example**  
```js
stackedBar().width(600).render('#chart', data);
```
## exports~StackedBarData : `Array.<Object>`
**Kind**: inner typedef of `exports`  
**Properties**

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| name | `String` | Name of the entry |
| stack | `String` | Stack of the entry |
| value | `Number` | Value of the entry |

**Example**  
```js
[
    {
        name: "2011-01",
        stack: "Direct",
        value: 0
    }
]
```

---

# Tooltip

Source: https://britecharts.github.io/britecharts/docs/API/tooltip

Tooltip component: one box, drawn inside the chart's svg, that follows the
pointer and shows what it is over. It renders a **list** (a title and one
row per topic, with a colour dot, the topic's name and its value) for the
multi-value charts -- line, stacked area, stacked bar and grouped bar --
or a **single value** (a title, the element's name and a big value) for
the single-value charts -- bar, scatter plot, heatmap and donut. By
default it picks the layout from the data point it is given; `layout()`
forces one. `miniTooltip` is this component with the single layout, an
empty title and a `.2f` number format.

The tooltip keeps itself inside the chart: it measures the svg it is drawn
in, sits beside its anchor, flips to the other side when there is no room
and slides so it is never cut off. It fades in when shown, fades out when
hidden and eases towards each new position.

Every chart dispatches the same three events, so wiring is always
`chart.on('customMouseOver', tooltip.show).on('customMouseMove', tooltip.update).on('customMouseOut', tooltip.hide)`.
What they carry, and where to `.call()` the tooltip:

| Chart | `customMouseOver` | `customMouseMove` | anchor `[x, y]` | attach to |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| line, stacked area | `(data, [x, y])` | `(dataPoint, [x, y], [width, height], colorMap)` | the hovered date's x, the pointer's y | `.metadata-group .vertical-marker-container` |
| stacked bar, grouped bar | `(data, [x, y])` | `(dataPoint, [x, y], [width, height], colorMap)` | the pointer, over a bar only | `.metadata-group` |
| bar, heatmap, donut | `(dataPoint, [x, y], [width, height])` | `(dataPoint, [x, y], [width, height])` | the pointer, over a shape only | `.metadata-group` |
| scatter plot | `(dataPoint, [x, y])` | `(dataPoint, [x, y], [width, height])` | the hovered point | `.metadata-group` |

Positions are in pixels relative to the chart's drawing area (inside the
margins). The chart's size is accepted and ignored: the tooltip measures
the chart itself. The line and stacked area charts dispatch nothing while
narrower than `tooltipThreshold` (480 px by default).

## Reading each chart's data point

The charts do not all name the fields of the data point they dispatch the
same way, so the tooltip has to be told where to look for some of them.
Without these settings, a tooltip on these charts shows no rows, rows
without their colours, or no value:

| Chart | Configure the tooltip with | Why |
| --- | --- | --- |
| line | nothing | its data point carries `date` and `topics`, the defaults |
| stacked area | `topicLabel('values')` | its rows are under `values` |
| stacked bar | `topicLabel('values')`, `nameLabel('stack')` | its rows are under `values`, named by `stack` |
| grouped bar | `topicLabel('values')`, `nameLabel('group')` | its rows are under `values`, named by `group` |
| scatter plot | `valueLabel('y')` | a point's value is its `y` (add `nameLabel('x')` to show `x` instead of its name) |
| bar, donut, heatmap | nothing | their data points carry `name` and `value` |

In React, `Tooltip` starts from `topicLabel('values')`, so the line chart
is the one that needs a setting there: `topicLabel="topics"`.

## miniTooltip, the single-value preset

`miniTooltip()` is `tooltip().layout('single').title('').numberFormat('.2f')`:
the same component with the single-value layout, no title and a `.2f`
number format, for the bar, scatter plot, heatmap and donut charts. Every
accessor documented on this page is available on it.

```js
const barChart = bar(),
    chartTooltip = miniTooltip();

barChart
    .width(500)
    .on('customMouseOver', chartTooltip.show)
    .on('customMouseMove', chartTooltip.update)
    .on('customMouseOut', chartTooltip.hide);

d3Selection.select('.css-selector')
    .datum(dataset)
    .call(barChart);

d3Selection.select('.metadata-group')
    .datum([])
    .call(chartTooltip);
```

**Example**  
```js
import { select } from 'd3-selection';
import { line, tooltip } from '@britecharts/core';

// dataset: { data: [{ topicName, name, date, value }] }
const lineChart = line();
const chartTooltip = tooltip().title('Tooltip title');

lineChart
    .width(500)
    .on('customMouseOver', chartTooltip.show)
    .on('customMouseMove', chartTooltip.update)
    .on('customMouseOut', chartTooltip.hide);

const container = select('.css-selector');

container.datum(dataset).call(lineChart);

// After the chart has drawn: the line chart's tooltip goes on its hover marker
container
    .select('.metadata-group .hover-marker')
    .datum([])
    .call(chartTooltip);
```

## exports(_selection, _data)
This function creates the graph using the selection as container

**Kind**: Exported function  

| Param | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| _selection | `D3Selection` | A d3 selection that represents                                  the container(s) where the chart(s) will be rendered |
| _data | `Object` | The data to attach and generate the chart |

## axisTimeCombinations
constants to be used to force the x axis to respect a certain granularity
current options: HOUR_DAY, DAY_MONTH, MONTH_YEAR

**Kind**: static property of `exports`  
**Example**  
```js
tooltip.dateFormat(tooltip.axisTimeCombinations.HOUR_DAY)
```
## dateFormat(_x) ⇒ `String` \| `module`
Exposes the ability to force the tooltip to use a certain date format

**Returns**: `String` \| `module` - Current format or module to chain calls  

| Param | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| _x | `String` | Desired format |

## dateCustomFormat(_x) ⇒ `String` \| `module`
Exposes the ability to use a custom date format

**Returns**: `String` \| `module` - Current format or module to chain calls  

| Param | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| _x | `String` | Desired custom format |

**Example**  
```js
tooltip.dateFormat(tooltip.axisTimeCombinations.CUSTOM);
tooltip.dateCustomFormat('%H:%M %p')
```
## dateLabel(_x) ⇒ `String` \| `module`
Gets or Sets the dateLabel of the data: the field of the data point
shown in the title. When the data point has no such field, its `key`
(what the stacked and grouped bar charts dispatch) or its `date` is
used, so the default works for every chart.

**Returns**: `String` \| `module` - Current dateLabel or Chart module to chain calls  

| Param | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| _x | `String` | Desired dateLabel |

## hide() ⇒ `module`
Hides the tooltip

**Returns**: `module` - Tooltip module to chain calls  
## locale(_x) ⇒ `String` \| `module`
Pass locale for the tooltip to render the date in

**Returns**: `String` \| `module` - Current locale or module to chain calls  

| Param | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| _x | `String` | Must be a locale tag like 'en-US' or 'fr-FR' |

## nameLabel(_x) ⇒ `String` \| `module`
Gets or Sets the nameLabel of the data: the field that identifies each
row of the list, and the colour the chart gave it, or the name shown in
the single layout. `'name'` by default. The stacked bar chart names its
rows by `stack` and the grouped bar chart by `group`: without
`nameLabel('stack')` or `nameLabel('group')`, the tooltip looks up each
row's colour under the bar's name, and the rows show none.

**Returns**: `String` \| `module` - Current nameLabel or Chart module to chain calls  

| Param | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| _x | `String` | Desired nameLabel |

## numberFormat(_x) ⇒ `string` \| `module`
Gets or Sets the number format for the value displayed on the tooltip

**Returns**: `string` \| `module` - Current numberFormat or Chart module to chain calls  

| Param | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| _x | `string` | Desired numberFormat for the chart. See examples [here](https://d3js.org/d3-format) |

## valueFormatter(_x) ⇒ `function` \| `module`
Gets or Sets the formatter function for the value displayed on the tooltip.
Setting this property makes the tooltip ignore numberFormat.

**Returns**: `function` \| `module` - Current valueFormatter or Chart module to chain calls  

| Param | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| _x | `function` | Desired formatter function |

**Example**  
```js
tooltipChart.valueFormatter(value => value.toString().length.toString())
```
## shouldShowDateInTitle(_x) ⇒ `Boolean` \| `module`
Gets or Sets shouldShowDateInTitle

**Returns**: `Boolean` \| `module` - Current shouldShowDateInTitle or Chart module to chain calls  

| Param | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| _x | `Boolean` | Desired value |

## show([dataPoint], [position]) ⇒ `module`
Shows the tooltip. Given the hovered data point and its position, as
the single-value charts dispatch them on `customMouseOver`, it renders
and places the tooltip at once; otherwise it shows empty until the
first `update`, which is what the multi-value charts need.

**Returns**: `module` - Tooltip module to chain calls  

| Param | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| [dataPoint] | `Object` | Data point to render |
| [position] | `Array.<Number>` | [x, y] to anchor the tooltip to, in pixels |

## title(_x) ⇒ `String` \| `module`
Gets or Sets the title of the tooltip (to only show the date, set a blank title)

**Returns**: `String` \| `module` - Current title or module to chain calls  

| Param | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| _x | `String` | Desired title |

## tooltipOffset(_x) ⇒ `Object` \| `module`
Gets or Sets an offset, in pixels, applied to the point the tooltip is
placed next to: `x` moves the anchor along the chart, `y` moves the box
up (negative) or down. The box still stays inside the chart.

**Returns**: `Object` \| `module` - Current tooltipOffset or module to chain calls  

| Param | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| _x | `Object` | Object with the x and y offsets |

**Example**  
```js
tooltip.tooltipOffset({ x: 0, y: -20 })
```
## layout([_x]) ⇒ `String` \| `module`
Gets or Sets the layout: 'list' shows the title and one row per topic,
with a colour dot, the topic's name and its value (the multi-value
charts: line, stacked area, stacked bar and grouped bar); 'single'
shows the title, the name and a big value (the single-value charts:
bar, scatter plot, heatmap and donut -- what `miniTooltip` renders);
'auto', the default, picks by the data point: a list when it carries
an array under the topic label, a single value otherwise. Set before
the tooltip is drawn.

**Returns**: `String` \| `module` - Current layout or Chart module to chain calls  

| Param | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| [_x] | `String` | `&#x27;auto&#x27;` | 'auto', 'list' or 'single' |

**Example**  
```js
tooltip.layout('single')
```
## maxEntries([_x]) ⇒ `Number` \| `module`
Gets or Sets the most rows the tooltip shows. Past that, the last row
reads "+n more" instead, so the box keeps a height that fits in the
chart. 0 shows every row.

**Returns**: `Number` \| `module` - Current maxEntries or Chart module to chain calls  

| Param | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| [_x] | `Number` | `12` | Most rows to show |

**Example**  
```js
tooltip.maxEntries(6)
```
## topicsOrder(_x) ⇒ `Array.<String>` \| `module`
Pass an override for the ordering of your tooltip

**Returns**: `Array.<String>` \| `module` - Current overrideOrder or Chart module to chain calls  

| Param | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| _x | `Array.<String>` | Array of the names of your tooltip items |

## topicLabel(_x) ⇒ `String` \| `module`
Gets or Sets the topicLabel of the data: the field of the data point
that holds the list's rows. `'topics'` by default, which is what the
line chart dispatches. The stacked area, stacked bar and grouped bar
charts dispatch their rows as `values`, so set `topicLabel('values')`
for them. (`@britecharts/wrappers`, and so React's `Tooltip`, set
`'values'` themselves: there, the line chart needs `'topics'`.)

**Returns**: `String` \| `module` - Current topicLabel or Chart module to chain calls  

| Param | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| _x | `String` | Desired topicLabel |

## update(dataPoint, position, [chartSize], [colorMap]) ⇒ `module`
Updates the content and position of the tooltip. The arguments are
what every chart dispatches with `customMouseMove`, so
`chart.on('customMouseMove', tooltip.update)` is all the wiring
needed: the data point, its anchor `[x, y]` in pixels relative to the
chart's drawing area, the chart's size (ignored; the tooltip measures
the chart itself) and, from the multi-value charts, the map of topic
names to colours. The order the multi-value charts used before 3.0,
`update(dataPoint, colorMap, x, y)`, still works and warns once.

**Returns**: `module` - Tooltip module to chain calls  

| Param | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| dataPoint | `Object` | Data point to render |
| position | `Array.<Number>` | [x, y] to anchor the tooltip to, in pixels |
| [chartSize] | `Array.<Number>` | [width, height] of the chart; ignored |
| [colorMap] | `Object` | Topic name to colour, for the list layout |

**Example**  
```js
chart.on('customMouseMove', tooltip.update)
```
## valueLabel(_x) ⇒ `String` \| `module`
Gets or Sets the valueLabel of the data: the field holding the value
shown for each row, or the big value of the single layout. `'value'`
by default. The scatter plot's points carry theirs as `y`, so set
`valueLabel('y')` for it.

**Returns**: `String` \| `module` - Current valueLabel or Chart module to chain calls  

| Param | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| _x | `String` | Desired valueLabel |

## xAxisValueType([_x]) ⇒ `String` \| `module`
Gets or Sets how the key of the data point is shown in the title:
'date' formats it as a date, 'number' as a number, 'category' shows
it as it is, and 'auto' (the default) picks one per key -- a Date or
a string that parses as one is a date, a number or a numeric string
is a number, anything else is a category. Set 'date' for keys that
happen to parse as numbers, or 'category' for names that happen to
parse as dates.

**Returns**: `String` \| `module` - Current xAxisValueType or Chart module to chain calls  

| Param | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| [_x] | `String` | `&#x27;auto&#x27;` | 'auto', 'date', 'number' or 'category' |

**Example**  
```js
tooltip.xAxisValueType('category')
```
